name.en: Battle of Shanhai Pass and fall of the Ming

summary.en: Weeks after Li Zicheng took Beijing and the Chongzhen Emperor hanged himself, the Ming general Wu Sangui opened Shanhai Pass to the Qing regent Dorgon; their combined forces routed Li, and the Qing moved its capital to Beijing.
summary.zh: 李自成攻破北京、崇祯帝自缢后，吴三桂开山海关降清，与多尔衮合击大顺军，清军入关，定都北京。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
赵尔巽等《清史稿》卷4 世祖本纪一 顺治元年
张廷玉等《明史》卷24 庄烈帝纪二

story.en:
On 25 April 1644 Li Zicheng's rebel army entered Beijing, and the Chongzhen Emperor hanged himself on Coal Hill behind the palace. The Ming's strongest remaining army, under Wu Sangui, stood at Shanhai Pass, where the Great Wall meets the sea, with the Manchu Qing on the other side.

Wu wavered, then refused to submit to Li, whose men had seized his family in Beijing. A famous later tradition, popularised by Wu Weiye's poem, says his rage was over the courtesan Chen Yuanyuan; historians treat this as embroidery. Wu appealed to the Qing regent Dorgon for help. On 27 May, as Li's army attacked Wu's lines outside the pass, Qing banner cavalry charged out of a sandstorm on the flank and routed the rebels.

Li fled back to Beijing, proclaimed himself emperor for a day and abandoned the city. On 6 June Dorgon entered Beijing, and that autumn the young Shunzhi Emperor was installed there. The Qing presented itself as avenging the Ming, but it went on to conquer the whole country, and Wu Sangui became its most powerful vassal in the southwest.
story.zh:
1644年4月25日，李自成的大顺军攻入北京，崇祯帝在宫后煤山自缢。明朝残存最强的一支军队由吴三桂统领，驻守长城入海处的山海关，关外即是清军。

吴三桂一度动摇，后因家人在北京被大顺军拘押而拒绝归附李自成。后世流传的说法（因吴伟业《圆圆曲》而广为人知）称他是为名妓陈圆圆“冲冠一怒”，史家多视之为文学渲染。吴三桂向清摄政王多尔衮求援。5月27日，大顺军猛攻关外吴军阵地时，清军八旗骑兵借风沙从侧翼突入，大顺军溃败。

李自成退回北京，匆忙称帝后即弃城西走。6月6日多尔衮进入北京，当年秋天顺治帝迁都于此。清廷以替明朝复仇为号召，却由此一统全国，吴三桂则成为雄踞西南的最强藩王。

name.en: Koxinga takes Taiwan from the Dutch

summary.en: Ming loyalist Zheng Chenggong (Koxinga) landed at Luermen and besieged the Dutch East India Company's Fort Zeelandia for nine months, forcing its surrender in February 1662 and founding a Zheng regime on Taiwan.
summary.zh: 明郑延平王郑成功自鹿耳门登陆，围攻荷兰东印度公司热兰遮城九个月，1662年2月荷军投降，郑氏据台。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
江日昇《台湾外记》
Britannica: Zheng Chenggong

story.en:
By 1661 Zheng Chenggong, the Ming loyalist known to Europeans as Koxinga, had been driven back to Xiamen after a failed assault on Nanjing. He needed a new base and turned to Taiwan, where the Dutch East India Company had ruled from Fort Zeelandia on the Tayouan sandbar since the 1620s.

On 30 April 1661 his fleet slipped through the shallow Luermen channel on a high tide, a route the Dutch thought impassable, and landed several thousand troops. Fort Provintia on the mainland surrendered within days, but Zeelandia, a stout bastioned fortress, held out. Zheng blockaded it, beat off a relief fleet from Batavia and, after a Dutch defector advised him, built batteries that pounded a key redoubt in January 1662.

Governor Frederick Coyett signed a surrender on 1 February 1662 and the Dutch sailed away. Zheng died that June, but his son and grandson ruled Taiwan as the Kingdom of Tungning until the Qing admiral Shi Lang took Penghu in 1683. Taiwan was then annexed to the Qing, and large-scale Chinese settlement followed.
story.zh:
1661年，被欧洲人称为“国姓爷”的明郑延平王郑成功北伐南京失利后退守厦门，急需新的根据地，于是把目光投向台湾。自17世纪20年代起，荷兰东印度公司便以大员沙洲上的热兰遮城统治台湾。

1661年4月30日，郑军船队趁大潮驶过荷兰人以为无法通航的鹿耳门水道，登陆数千兵马。本岛上的普罗民遮城数日内投降，但棱堡坚固的热兰遮城坚守不下。郑成功长期围困，击退从巴达维亚来援的舰队，又在荷兰降兵的建议下修筑炮台，于1662年1月轰击城外要塞。

1662年2月1日，荷兰长官揆一签约投降，荷兰人撤离台湾。郑成功当年六月去世，其子郑经、其孙郑克塽以东宁王国名义继续治台，直至1683年清将施琅攻取澎湖。台湾随即归入清朝版图，大规模的汉人移民也随之而来。

summary.en: When the Kangxi Emperor moved to abolish their fiefs, Wu Sangui in Yunnan and the princes in Guangdong and Fujian rebelled. After eight years of war Qing forces took Kunming in 1681.
summary.zh: 康熙帝下令撤藩，吴三桂于云南起兵，广东尚氏、福建耿氏响应；历时八年，1681年清军攻克昆明平定。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
赵尔巽等《清史稿》卷474 吴三桂传

story.en:
After the conquest the Qing rewarded three Chinese generals with near-independent fiefs in the south: Wu Sangui in Yunnan and Guizhou, Shang Kexi in Guangdong and Geng Jingzhong in Fujian. They ran their own armies and taxes and drew huge subsidies from Beijing. In 1673 Shang asked to retire to Manchuria, and the 19-year-old Kangxi Emperor, against the advice of most ministers, accepted and ordered all three fiefs dissolved.

Wu Sangui rose at the end of that year, soon styling himself King of Zhou, and Geng and later Shang's son joined him. For several years rebels held most of the south and the west, and Kangxi faced the real prospect of losing half the empire. He held his nerve, relied increasingly on Chinese Green Standard troops and commanders, and won back Geng and Shang through negotiation.

Wu Sangui declared himself emperor at Hengzhou in 1678 and died months later. Qing armies closed on Kunming, and in 1681 his grandson Wu Shifan killed himself as the city fell. The victory left Kangxi master of the whole country; two years later the Qing took Taiwan.
story.zh:
入关后，清廷把南方封给三位汉人降将，形同割据：吴三桂镇云贵，尚可喜镇广东，耿精忠镇福建。三藩自掌兵马钱粮，每年还向朝廷索取巨额军饷。1673年尚可喜请求归老辽东，年仅十九岁的康熙帝不顾多数大臣反对，准其所请，并下令三藩一并撤销。

同年年底吴三桂起兵，自称周王，耿精忠及后来尚可喜之子尚之信相继响应。数年间叛军占据南方和西部大片地区，康熙帝一度面临半壁江山不保的危局。他沉着应对，日益倚重绿营汉军与汉人将领，并通过招抚争取耿、尚二藩归降。

1678年吴三桂在衡州称帝，数月后病死。清军合围昆明，1681年城破之际，其孙吴世璠自尽。平定三藩使康熙帝真正掌控全国；两年后，清朝又收复台湾。

summary.en: After Qing forces besieged the Russian fort of Albazin, envoys led by Songgotu signed China's first treaty with a European state at Nerchinsk, fixing the border along the Argun river and the Stanovoy range.
summary.zh: 清军两次围攻雅克萨后，索额图与俄使在尼布楚签订条约，以额尔古纳河与外兴安岭划定中俄东段边界，是中国与欧洲国家的首个条约。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
赵尔巽等《清史稿》卷7 圣祖本纪二 康熙二十八年
Britannica: Treaty of Nerchinsk

story.en:
In the mid-17th century Russian Cossacks pushed down the Amur and built a fort at Albazin, clashing with Qing subjects and tributaries. Once the south was secure the Kangxi Emperor turned north. Qing troops took Albazin in 1685; when the Russians returned and rebuilt it, they besieged it again in 1686 until Moscow asked to negotiate.

In August 1689 the two embassies met at Nerchinsk, beyond Lake Baikal. The Qing side was led by the Manchu grandee Songgotu with an imposing escort; the Russian envoy was Fyodor Golovin. Neither side spoke the other's language, so the talks ran through two Jesuits in Qing service, Thomas Pereira and Jean-François Gerbillon, in Latin, and the authoritative text was the Latin one.

Signed on 7 September 1689, the treaty set the border along the Argun river and the Stanovoy range, removed Albazin and allowed trade with passports. It was China's first treaty with a European state and was concluded between equals. It held for 170 years, until Russia used the Qing's weakness during the Second Opium War to take the lands north of the Amur and east of the Ussuri.
story.zh:
17世纪中叶，沙俄哥萨克沿黑龙江南下，在雅克萨筑城，与清朝属民屡起冲突。南方平定后，康熙帝把目光转向北方。1685年清军攻克雅克萨；俄军返回重建城堡后，清军于1686年再度围城，直至莫斯科请求议和。

1689年8月，双方使团在贝加尔湖以东的尼布楚会晤。清方以满洲重臣索额图为首，随行兵马声势浩大；俄方全权代表为戈洛文。两国语言不通，谈判经由在清廷供职的耶稣会士徐日升和张诚以拉丁文进行，条约也以拉丁文本为准。

条约于1689年9月7日签订，以额尔古纳河和外兴安岭为界，拆毁雅克萨城，并允许持照贸易。这是中国与欧洲国家签订的第一个条约，双方地位平等。它维持了一百七十年，直到第二次鸦片战争期间沙俄趁清朝衰弱，夺走黑龙江以北和乌苏里江以东的土地。

summary.en: The Qianlong Emperor's Complete Library of the Four Treasuries copied some 3,500 works into about 36,000 volumes, while the same review suppressed and destroyed thousands of books judged seditious.
summary.zh: 乾隆帝开四库全书馆，抄录典籍约三千五百种、三万六千余册；修书同时禁毁大量“违碍”书籍。

《四库全书总目》卷首 圣谕
Britannica: Siku quanshu

note: The first set was completed in 1782; Wikidata gives 1773–1783.

summary.en: Britain's first embassy to China, led by George Macartney, was received by the Qianlong Emperor at the Chengde summer palace, but its requests for trade concessions and a permanent embassy were refused.
summary.zh: 英国首个访华使团由马戛尔尼率领，于承德避暑山庄觐见乾隆帝，其通商与驻使要求均遭拒绝。

Britannica: George Macartney
《清高宗实录》乾隆五十八年八月

summary.en: Imperial commissioner Lin Zexu confiscated over 20,000 chests of British opium in Canton and destroyed it on the beach at Humen over 23 days, a confrontation that led directly to the First Opium War.
summary.zh: 钦差大臣林则徐收缴英商鸦片两万余箱，于虎门海滩历时二十三天当众销毁，直接引发第一次鸦片战争。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
赵尔巽等《清史稿》卷369 林则徐传

story.en:
By the 1830s British and American merchants were smuggling tens of thousands of chests of Indian opium into China every year, and silver was flowing out to pay for it. The Daoguang Emperor chose Lin Zexu, a governor-general known for honesty, as imperial commissioner to stamp out the trade. Lin reached Canton in March 1839, blockaded the foreign factories and refused to let the merchants leave until they handed over their stocks.

The British superintendent of trade, Charles Elliot, eventually surrendered 20,283 chests, promising the merchants compensation from London. Rather than burn the drug, which would leave a residue that could be recovered, Lin had pits dug on the beach at Humen. From 3 June workers broke the opium into pits of brine, added lime to dissolve it and flushed the sludge out to sea on the tide. It took 23 days. Lin even composed a prayer asking the spirits of the sea to forgive the poison.

London treated the seizure of British-held property as an outrage. Elliot's compensation promise turned the merchants' loss into a government debt, and the cabinet sent a fleet in 1840.
story.zh:
到19世纪30年代，英美商人每年向中国走私数万箱印度鸦片，白银随之大量外流。道光帝任命以清廉著称的湖广总督林则徐为钦差大臣，前往广东禁烟。林则徐于1839年3月抵达广州，封锁外国商馆，勒令商人交出全部存烟，否则不准离开。

英国驻华商务总监义律最终交出鸦片二万零二百八十三箱，并以英国政府名义许诺赔偿商人损失。林则徐没有采用焚烧之法，因为焚后残膏仍可回收。他命人在虎门海滩挖池，自6月3日起将烟土切碎投入盐水池中，再撒入石灰使之溶解，趁退潮将渣沫冲入大海，前后历时二十三天。林则徐还撰写祭文，向海神致歉，请海中生灵暂避毒物。

英国政府视收缴英商财产为奇耻大辱。义律的赔偿承诺把商人的损失变成了政府的债务，英国内阁遂于1840年派出远征舰队。

summary.en: Britain sent an expeditionary force after the opium seizures; steam warships blockaded the coast, took Zhoushan, Xiamen and Zhenjiang and threatened Nanjing, forcing the Qing to sue for peace.
summary.zh: 英国以禁烟为由派远征军来华，封锁沿海，攻占定海、厦门、镇江，兵临南京，清廷被迫求和。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
Britannica: Opium Wars
《筹办夷务始末》道光朝

note: Jiangshan-map dates the war from the 1840 British expedition; Wikidata starts it in March 1839 with Lin Zexu's blockade.

story.en:
In June 1840 a British expeditionary force arrived off Canton. Instead of attacking Lin Zexu's fortified river, it sailed north, took Dinghai on Zhoushan island and appeared off Tianjin, alarming the court. The Daoguang Emperor dismissed Lin and sent Qishan to negotiate, but the Chuanbi Convention of January 1841, which promised Hong Kong to Britain, was repudiated by both governments.

The fighting resumed. Steam-powered gunboats such as the iron-hulled Nemesis outclassed Qing war junks, and Qing shore batteries were repeatedly outflanked. Near Canton in May 1841 villagers of Sanyuanli surrounded a British detachment in a rainstorm, an episode later celebrated as popular resistance. In 1841–42 the British took Xiamen, Ningbo and Zhapu, then entered the Yangtze. At Zhenjiang in July 1842 the Manchu garrison fought to the last and many of its families killed themselves rather than be captured.

With the Grand Canal cut and British ships off Nanjing, the court sued for peace. The war exposed the gap between Qing and Western military technology and opened a century of treaties imposed by force.
story.zh:
1840年6月，英国远征军抵达广州洋面。英军没有进攻林则徐严密设防的珠江口，而是挥师北上，攻占舟山定海，又驶抵天津大沽口外，令朝廷震动。道光帝将林则徐革职，派琦善议和，但1841年1月议定、许诺割让香港的《穿鼻草约》被两国政府同时否认。

战事再起。“复仇女神”号铁壳蒸汽舰等英国炮舰远胜清军木制战船，清军炮台屡屡被迂回攻破。1841年5月，广州城北三元里乡民趁大雨围困一支英军，此事后来被视为民众抗英的象征。1841至1842年间，英军先后攻占厦门、宁波、乍浦，随后进入长江。1842年7月镇江之战中，八旗驻防兵死战到底，许多旗人家眷宁死不降。

大运河漕运被切断、英舰兵临南京城下，清廷被迫求和。这场战争暴露了清朝与西方在军事技术上的巨大差距，开启了列强以武力强加条约的一个世纪。

summary.en: Signed aboard HMS Cornwallis off Nanjing, the treaty ceded Hong Kong Island to Britain, opened five treaty ports and imposed an indemnity – the first of the "unequal treaties".
summary.zh: 在南京江面英舰“康华丽”号上签订，割让香港岛，开放广州、厦门、福州、宁波、上海五口通商并赔款，为第一个不平等条约。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
Britannica: Treaty of Nanjing
《中外旧约章汇编》第一册

story.en:
By August 1842 British warships lay in the Yangtze below Nanjing and troops were ready to storm the city. The Daoguang Emperor authorised the Manchu officials Qiying and Yilibu to accept terms. On 29 August they signed the treaty with Sir Henry Pottinger aboard HMS Cornwallis.

Its 13 articles ceded Hong Kong Island to Britain in perpetuity, opened Canton, Xiamen, Fuzhou, Ningbo and Shanghai to British residence and trade, abolished the licensed Cohong merchant monopoly and imposed an indemnity of 21 million silver dollars, partly to pay for the opium Lin Zexu had destroyed. The treaty itself did not mention opium, which remained illegal in China but continued to pour in.

A supplementary treaty in 1843 added consular jurisdiction over British subjects and a most-favoured-nation clause, and the United States and France soon obtained similar treaties. Chinese historians call these the first "unequal treaties", and the date of 1842 traditionally opens China's modern history. Shanghai, a modest county town, began its rise into one of Asia's greatest ports.
story.zh:
1842年8月，英国军舰已停泊在南京城下的长江江面，英军准备攻城。道光帝授权满洲官员耆英、伊里布接受条件。8月29日，二人与璞鼎查在英舰“康华丽”号上签订条约。

条约共十三款：将香港岛永久割让给英国；开放广州、厦门、福州、宁波、上海五处为通商口岸，准许英人居住贸易；废除公行垄断；赔款二千一百万银元，其中一部分用于偿付被林则徐销毁的鸦片。条约本身对鸦片只字未提，鸦片在中国仍属违禁，却依旧源源流入。

1843年的《虎门条约》又增加了领事裁判权和片面最惠国待遇，美国、法国随即签订类似条约。中国史学界称之为第一个不平等条约，并传统上以1842年作为中国近代史的开端。当时不过是普通县城的上海，由此开始崛起为亚洲最重要的港口之一。

summary.en: Hong Xiuquan's God Worshippers rose at Jintian in Guangxi, marched north and made Nanjing their Heavenly Capital in 1853. Internal purges and the Xiang Army of Zeng Guofan ended the movement in 1864; perhaps 20 million died.
summary.zh: 洪秀全领导拜上帝会于广西金田起义，1853年定都天京。天京事变后由盛转衰，1864年为曾国藩湘军所灭，死难者或达二千万。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
Britannica: Taiping Rebellion
赵尔巽等《清史稿》卷475 洪秀全传

note: Wikidata's point in time is 1850 (mobilisation at Jintian); the formal uprising was proclaimed on 11 January 1851, as in Jiangshan-map.

story.en:
Hong Xiuquan, a Hakka village teacher from near Guangzhou, failed the civil-service examinations repeatedly. After a breakdown in 1837 he had visions which he later interpreted, with the help of a Christian tract by Liang Fa, as revealing that he was the younger brother of Jesus sent to destroy demons. His God Worshipping Society spread among poor Hakka and miners in Guangxi, and on 11 January 1851 it rose at Jintian and proclaimed the Heavenly Kingdom of Great Peace.

The Taiping army swept down the Xiang and Yangtze rivers and took Nanjing in March 1853, renaming it Tianjing. It banned opium, foot-binding and concubinage on paper and segregated men and women. In 1856 the leadership tore itself apart: the Eastern King Yang Xiuqing was murdered with thousands of followers, and Shi Dakai led his army away.

The Qing relied on new provincial armies, above all Zeng Guofan's Hunan (Xiang) Army, later aided by Western-officered units. Hong died in June 1864 and Nanjing fell a few weeks later amid massacre. The war devastated the lower Yangtze; most estimates of the dead range from 20 to 30 million.
story.zh:
洪秀全是广州附近的客家村塾先生，屡试不第。1837年他大病一场，梦见异象，后来借助梁发所著基督教小册子《劝世良言》，认定自己是上帝次子、耶稣之弟，奉命下凡斩妖除魔。他创立的拜上帝会在广西贫苦客家人和矿工中迅速传播，1851年1月11日在金田起义，建号“太平天国”。

太平军沿湘江、长江一路东下，1853年3月攻克南京，改称天京。太平天国在纸面上禁止鸦片、缠足和纳妾，并实行男女分营。1856年领导层内讧，东王杨秀清及其部众数千人被杀，翼王石达开率部出走，史称“天京事变”。

清廷依靠新兴的地方武装，首推曾国藩的湘军，后又有洋人统带的洋枪队相助。1864年6月洪秀全病逝，数周后天京陷落，城中遭到屠戮。战争使长江下游残破不堪，多数估计死亡人数在二千万至三千万之间。

name.en: Second Opium War and burning of the Old Summer Palace
name.zh: 第二次鸦片战争与火烧圆明园

summary.en: Britain and France fought the Qing over trade and diplomatic access; in 1860 their troops entered Beijing and burned the Yuanmingyuan. The Conventions of Peking opened more ports and ceded Kowloon, while Russia gained the lands east of the Ussuri.
summary.zh: 英法以修约为由对清开战，1860年联军攻入北京，劫掠焚毁圆明园；《北京条约》增开口岸、割九龙司，沙俄趁机攫取乌苏里江以东地区。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
Britannica: Opium Wars
赵尔巽等《清史稿》卷20 文宗本纪 咸丰十年

story.en:
In October 1856 Canton officials seized the Arrow, a Chinese-owned ship that had been registered in Hong Kong, and Britain used the incident to press for treaty revision. France joined after the execution of a missionary. Allied forces took Canton in 1857 and the Dagu forts in 1858, and the Treaties of Tianjin opened new ports, legalised opium imports and allowed foreign envoys to live in Beijing.

When the British and French returned in 1859 to ratify the treaties, the Dagu forts repulsed them. In 1860 a larger force landed, and during negotiations the Qing seized the envoy Harry Parkes and his party; about twenty of the captives died. The Xianfeng Emperor fled to Chengde. In October, in retaliation, Lord Elgin ordered the burning of the Yuanmingyuan, the vast imperial garden palace northwest of Beijing, which troops had already looted.

Prince Gong signed the Conventions of Peking, which ceded Kowloon and added indemnities. The Russian envoy Ignatiev, posing as mediator, gained the territory east of the Ussuri. The shock pushed the court towards the Self-Strengthening Movement and a foreign office, the Zongli Yamen.
story.zh:
1856年10月，广东官员在一艘曾在香港登记的华人商船“亚罗”号上缉拿水手，英国借此要求修约。法国则以马神甫被杀为由加入。英法联军于1857年攻占广州，1858年攻陷大沽炮台，《天津条约》增开口岸，使鸦片贸易合法化，并允许外国公使驻京。

1859年英法使节北上换约时，被大沽炮台守军击退。1860年联军大举登陆，谈判期间清方扣押英国使节巴夏礼一行，被扣者约二十人死亡。咸丰帝逃往热河承德。10月，额尔金下令焚毁北京西北的皇家园林圆明园作为报复，此前园中珍宝已遭联军大肆劫掠。

恭亲王奕訢签订《北京条约》，割让九龙司并增加赔款。以“调停人”自居的俄国公使伊格纳季耶夫则攫取了乌苏里江以东的大片领土。这一冲击促使清廷设立总理各国事务衙门，开启了洋务运动。

summary.en: Zeng Guofan and Li Hongzhang founded the Jiangnan Arsenal in Shanghai, the largest enterprise of the Self-Strengthening Movement; it built steamships and guns and translated Western science texts.
summary.zh: 曾国藩、李鸿章在上海创办江南机器制造总局，为洋务运动最大的军工企业，造船造炮并设翻译馆译介西学。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
Britannica: Self-Strengthening Movement
赵尔巽等《清史稿》卷411 李鸿章传

summary.en: Fought over Korea, the war saw Japan destroy the Beiyang Fleet at the Yalu and Weihaiwei. In the Treaty of Shimonoseki China recognised Korean independence and ceded Taiwan, Penghu and (briefly) Liaodong.
summary.zh: 中日因朝鲜问题开战，北洋舰队在黄海、威海卫覆没。《马关条约》中国承认朝鲜“独立”，割让台湾、澎湖及辽东半岛（后赎回）。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
Britannica: First Sino-Japanese War
赵尔巽等《清史稿》卷24 德宗本纪二

story.en:
Korea was a Qing tributary, but Meiji Japan wanted it in its own sphere. When the Donghak peasant uprising broke out in 1894, both powers sent troops, and on 25 July Japan sank a British-flagged transport carrying Chinese soldiers. The war that followed tested the modernised forces each had built since the 1860s.

On 17 September the Beiyang Fleet met the Japanese navy off the mouth of the Yalu. The cruiser Zhiyuan, under Captain Deng Shichang, tried to ram the Yoshino and was sunk with almost all hands. Faster, better-handled Japanese ships won the day, and on land Japanese armies took Pyongyang, crossed into Manchuria and captured Port Arthur. In February 1895 the remaining Chinese ships were trapped at Weihaiwei; Admiral Ding Ruchang refused Japanese calls to surrender and took his own life, after which his subordinates gave up the ships.

Li Hongzhang negotiated the Treaty of Shimonoseki after being shot and wounded by a Japanese gunman. China recognised Korean independence, ceded Taiwan and Penghu and paid 200 million taels; Russia, France and Germany forced Japan to return Liaodong. The defeat exposed the limits of Self-Strengthening and set off a scramble for concessions.
story.zh:
朝鲜是清朝的藩属国，明治日本却想把它纳入自己的势力范围。1894年朝鲜爆发东学党起义，中日两国都出兵朝鲜。7月25日，日舰击沉了运送清军的英籍商船“高升”号。随之而来的战争，检验了两国自19世纪60年代以来各自建设的新式军队。

9月17日，北洋舰队与日本联合舰队在鸭绿江口外的黄海海面交战。邓世昌指挥的“致远”舰欲撞击日舰“吉野”，不幸沉没，舰上官兵几乎全部殉国。速度更快、指挥更得当的日本舰队占据上风；陆上日军攻占平壤，越过鸭绿江进入东北，攻陷旅顺。1895年2月，北洋舰队残部被困威海卫，提督丁汝昌拒降后服毒自尽，舰队随即投降。

李鸿章赴日议和期间遭日本刺客小山丰太郎枪击受伤，最终签订《马关条约》：中国承认朝鲜“独立”，割让台湾、澎湖，赔款二亿两白银；俄、法、德三国干涉，迫使日本归还辽东半岛。这场惨败暴露了洋务运动的局限，并引发列强瓜分中国的狂潮。

name.zh: 义和团运动与八国联军

summary.en: Anti-foreign Boxer militias besieged the Beijing legations with court support in 1900; an eight-nation expeditionary force took the city, the Empress Dowager fled to Xi'an, and the Boxer Protocol imposed a vast indemnity.
summary.zh: 义和团在清廷纵容下围攻北京使馆区，八国联军攻占北京，慈禧挟光绪西逃；1901年《辛丑条约》赔款四亿五千万两。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
Britannica: Boxer Rebellion
赵尔巽等《清史稿》卷24 德宗本纪二 光绪二十六年

story.en:
The Boxers United in Righteousness arose in drought-stricken Shandong in 1898–99. They practised martial rituals that, they believed, made them invulnerable to bullets, and they attacked Chinese Christians, missionaries and railways. Their slogan "Support the Qing, destroy the foreign" won sympathy at court, and in June 1900 thousands poured into Beijing and Tianjin.

On 20 June the German minister Clemens von Ketteler was shot in the street, and the next day the Empress Dowager Cixi declared war on the foreign powers. For 55 days Boxers and imperial troops besieged the legation quarter and the Northern Cathedral, where diplomats, Chinese Christians and soldiers held out behind improvised barricades. In the south, governors-general such as Zhang Zhidong and Liu Kunyi ignored the declaration and struck a "mutual protection" pact with the foreign consuls.

An eight-nation force relieved the legations on 14 August; Cixi fled to Xi'an with the Guangxu Emperor, and foreign troops looted the capital and launched punitive raids. The Boxer Protocol of 1901 imposed an indemnity of 450 million taels. The débâcle finally pushed the court into the New Policies reforms.
story.zh:
义和团于1898至1899年间兴起于旱灾肆虐的山东。拳民习练拳术和符咒，自信“刀枪不入”，攻击中国教民、传教士和铁路。“扶清灭洋”的口号赢得朝中部分权贵的支持，1900年6月大批拳民涌入北京、天津。

6月20日，德国公使克林德在街头被枪杀；次日慈禧太后向各国宣战。此后五十五天里，义和团和清军围攻东交民巷使馆区和北堂，外交官、中国教民和士兵依靠临时工事坚守。在南方，张之洞、刘坤一等督抚不奉宣战诏令，与各国领事议定“东南互保”。

8月14日，八国联军攻入北京解围；慈禧挟光绪帝西逃西安，联军在京城大肆劫掠，并四出“讨伐”。1901年签订的《辛丑条约》规定赔款白银四亿五千万两。这场惨败最终迫使清廷推行“清末新政”。

summary.en: Revolutionary soldiers of the New Army rose at Wuchang on 10 October 1911 and took the Hubei capital; within weeks most provinces declared independence from the Qing.
summary.zh: 1911年10月10日湖北新军革命党人在武昌起义，占领武汉三镇，各省纷纷响应宣布独立。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
Britannica: Wuchang Uprising
中国第一历史档案馆编《辛亥革命档案史料》

story.en:
By 1911 revolutionary societies such as the Literary Society and the Progressive Association had recruited thousands of soldiers in Hubei's modern New Army. On 9 October a bomb being assembled in the Russian concession at Hankou went off by accident. Police raided the building and seized membership lists, and several leaders were arrested and executed.

Facing exposure, soldiers of the engineering battalion at Wuchang rose on the evening of 10 October, seized the arsenal and attacked the governor-general's office. The governor-general fled, and by the next morning the city was in revolutionary hands. Lacking a senior figure, the rebels made the brigade commander Li Yuanhong military governor; by popular account he had to be found hiding and was persuaded only with difficulty.

Hanyang and Hankou soon followed. Sun Yat-sen, the movement's best-known leader, was in the United States raising funds and learned of the rising from a newspaper. Within about seven weeks fifteen provinces had declared independence from the Qing. The date, the "Double Ten", is still celebrated as National Day in Taiwan.
story.zh:
到1911年，文学社、共进会等革命团体已在湖北新军中发展了数千名成员。10月9日，革命党人在汉口俄租界秘密配制炸弹时意外爆炸，巡捕搜出党人名册，数名骨干被捕遇害。

面临暴露的危险，驻武昌的新军工程第八营士兵于10月10日晚率先发难，夺取楚望台军械库，进攻湖广总督署。总督瑞澂弃城而逃，次日清晨武昌已为革命军所控制。起义者缺乏有声望的领袖，便推举协统黎元洪为湖北军政府都督；据流传的说法，他被人从藏身处找出，几经劝说才勉强就任。

汉阳、汉口随即光复。革命党最著名的领袖孙中山当时正在美国筹款，从报纸上得知起义消息。约六周内，十五个省份宣布脱离清廷独立。10月10日“双十节”至今在台湾作为国庆日纪念。

name.en: Xinhai Revolution and founding of the Republic
name.zh: 辛亥革命与中华民国成立

summary.en: Sun Yat-sen was inaugurated as provisional president of the Republic of China in Nanjing on 1 January 1912; on 12 February the child emperor Puyi abdicated, ending over two thousand years of imperial rule.
summary.zh: 1912年1月1日孙中山在南京就任中华民国临时大总统；2月12日清帝溥仪退位，两千多年帝制终结。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
Britannica: Chinese Revolution (1911–12)
《清帝逊位诏书》（1912年2月12日）

story.en:
After the Wuchang rising the Qing court recalled the retired general Yuan Shikai, who controlled the Beiyang Army, and he fought the revolutionaries to a standstill while negotiating with both sides. Sun Yat-sen returned from abroad in late December 1911, and delegates of the independent provinces elected him provisional president.

On 1 January 1912 Sun took office in Nanjing and proclaimed the Republic of China, adopting the solar calendar. The revolutionaries lacked the armed strength to march north, however, and Sun agreed to stand aside for Yuan if he secured the end of the dynasty. Yuan pressed the court, and on 12 February the Empress Dowager Longyu issued the abdication edict on behalf of the six-year-old Puyi. Generous terms let Puyi keep his title and live in the Forbidden City.

Sun resigned, and on 10 March Yuan was inaugurated in Beijing as provisional president. The revolution ended more than two thousand years of imperial rule with relatively little bloodshed, but it did not settle who held power: within four years Yuan had tried to make himself emperor, and China fell into the warlord era.
story.zh:
武昌起义后，清廷起用赋闲在家、掌握北洋军的袁世凯。袁一面与革命军相持，一面与南北双方周旋。1911年12月下旬孙中山从海外归国，独立各省代表推选他为临时大总统。

1912年1月1日，孙中山在南京就职，宣告中华民国成立，改用阳历。然而革命军无力北伐，孙中山表示只要袁世凯促成清帝退位，就让出总统之位。袁世凯向清廷施压，2月12日隆裕太后以六岁的宣统帝溥仪名义颁布退位诏书。优待条件允许溥仪保留尊号、暂居紫禁城。

孙中山随即辞职，3月10日袁世凯在北京就任临时大总统。辛亥革命以相对较小的流血结束了两千多年的帝制，却没有解决权力归属问题：不到四年，袁世凯便图谋称帝，中国随后陷入军阀混战时代。

summary.en: Beijing students protested the Paris Peace Conference decision to give Germany's Shandong concessions to Japan; the demonstrations grew into a nationwide movement for science, democracy and vernacular culture.
summary.zh: 北京学生抗议巴黎和会将德国在山东权益转让日本，示威扩展为全国运动，推动了以科学、民主与白话文为旗帜的新文化运动。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
Britannica: May Fourth Movement
中共中央党史和文献研究院《中国共产党一百年大事记》

story.en:
China had joined the Allies in the First World War, sending some 140,000 labourers to France, and expected to recover the German concessions in Shandong. Instead, the Paris Peace Conference awarded them to Japan, and it emerged that the Beijing government had secretly agreed to Japanese claims in 1918.

On 4 May 1919 some 3,000 students from thirteen Beijing colleges marched to Tiananmen. Frustrated at the legation quarter, they went on to the house of the transport minister Cao Rulin, set it on fire and beat the envoy Zhang Zongxiang, whom they found there. Mass arrests followed, but the protest spread: in early June Shanghai merchants closed their shops and workers struck. The government dismissed the three officials blamed, and China's delegates refused to sign the Treaty of Versailles.

The name "May Fourth" came to stand for the wider New Culture Movement, which had begun with Chen Duxiu's magazine New Youth in 1915: "Mr Democracy and Mr Science", writing in the vernacular as Hu Shi urged and Lu Xun practised, and attacks on Confucian family ethics. Both the Nationalists and the Communists traced their intellectual roots to it.
story.zh:
中国在第一次世界大战中加入协约国，派往法国的华工约十四万人，本指望收回德国在山东的权益。巴黎和会却决定将其转让给日本，人们还得知北京政府在1918年曾秘密同意日本的要求。

1919年5月4日，北京十三所大专院校约三千名学生在天安门集会游行。他们在东交民巷使馆区受阻后，转往交通总长曹汝霖的住宅赵家楼，放火焚烧，并痛打了恰在那里的驻日公使章宗祥。北洋政府大批逮捕学生，抗议却迅速蔓延：6月初上海商人罢市、工人罢工。政府被迫罢免曹汝霖、章宗祥、陆宗舆三人，中国代表也拒绝在对德和约上签字。

“五四”后来成为更广泛的新文化运动的代名词。这一运动始于1915年陈独秀创办的《新青年》，倡导“德先生”与“赛先生”，提倡胡适所主张、鲁迅所实践的白话文学，并批判儒家礼教。国共两党都把自己的思想源头追溯到五四。

name.en: First National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party

summary.en: Thirteen delegates, including Mao Zedong, met secretly in Shanghai's French Concession, finishing on a boat on South Lake in Jiaxing, to found the Chinese Communist Party.
summary.zh: 包括毛泽东在内的十三名代表在上海法租界秘密集会，后转至嘉兴南湖游船上闭幕，宣告中国共产党成立。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
中共中央党史和文献研究院《中国共产党一百年大事记》
Britannica: Chinese Communist Party

story.en:
Marxism attracted Chinese radicals after the Russian Revolution and the disappointment of May Fourth. In 1920 Chen Duxiu in Shanghai and Li Dazhao in Beijing, helped by Comintern envoys, set up communist groups in several cities. In July 1921 these groups, with perhaps fifty members in all, sent thirteen delegates to Shanghai, joined by the Comintern representatives Maring and Nikolsky.

The congress opened on 23 July in a house on Wangzhi Road in the French Concession. Neither Chen nor Li attended. On 30 July a stranger looked into the meeting room, and soon afterwards the concession police searched the house. The delegates had already scattered, and they finished the congress on a hired tourist boat on South Lake at Jiaxing, posing as a pleasure party. They adopted a programme committed to proletarian revolution and chose Chen Duxiu as secretary in his absence.

The party grew slowly until it allied with the Nationalists in 1923. Of the thirteen delegates, some later left or were expelled, and a few collaborated with Japan; Mao Zedong, then a young teacher from Hunan, eventually led it to power. The party marks its founding on 1 July.
story.zh:
俄国十月革命和五四运动的失望之后，马克思主义吸引了一批中国激进知识分子。1920年，上海的陈独秀和北京的李大钊在共产国际代表协助下，先后在多个城市成立共产主义小组。1921年7月，这些总共约五十名成员的小组派出十三名代表来到上海，共产国际代表马林和尼克尔斯基也出席了会议。

7月23日，大会在法租界望志路的一处民宅开幕，陈独秀和李大钊均未到会。7月30日，一名陌生男子闯入会场张望，不久法租界巡捕前来搜查，代表们此前已经分散离开。他们随后转移到嘉兴南湖，在一条租来的游船上以游湖为掩护完成了会议，通过了以无产阶级革命为目标的纲领，并选举未到会的陈独秀为中央局书记。

此后党组织发展缓慢，直至1923年与国民党合作。十三名代表中，后来有人脱党或被开除，也有人投靠日本；当时还是湖南青年教师的毛泽东，最终领导这个党夺取了政权。中共以7月1日为建党纪念日。

summary.en: The Nationalist army under Chiang Kai-shek marched north from Guangzhou, defeating the Beiyang warlords; after the 1927 split with the Communists it took Beijing in 1928, and Zhang Xueliang's Manchuria joined the Nanjing government.
summary.zh: 蒋介石率国民革命军自广州誓师北伐，击败北洋军阀；1927年国共分裂，1928年克北京，张学良东北易帜，南京国民政府形式上统一全国。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
Britannica: Northern Expedition

story.en:
After Sun Yat-sen's death in 1925 the Nationalists, allied with the Communists and advised by Soviet officers, controlled only Guangdong. On 9 July 1926 Chiang Kai-shek, commandant of the Whampoa Military Academy, led the National Revolutionary Army north to defeat the warlords who held the Beijing government.

The campaign moved fast: Wuhan fell in October, and Shanghai and Nanjing in March 1927, helped by peasant and labour movements organised by Communists. But the coalition was splitting. On 12 April 1927 Chiang turned on the Communists and their unions in Shanghai, killing many, and set up his own government in Nanjing; the left-wing government in Wuhan expelled its Communists a few months later.

Chiang resumed the drive north in 1928. As Nationalist forces approached, the Manchurian warlord Zhang Zuolin withdrew from Beijing and was killed on 4 June when Japanese Kwantung Army officers blew up his train. Beijing was taken and renamed Beiping, and on 29 December 1928 Zhang's son Zhang Xueliang raised the Nationalist flag over Manchuria. China was nominally reunified under Nanjing, though many warlords kept their armies.
story.zh:
1925年孙中山逝世后，与共产党合作、由苏联顾问协助的国民党仅控制广东一省。1926年7月9日，黄埔军校校长蒋介石率国民革命军誓师北伐，讨伐控制北京政府的北洋军阀。

北伐进展迅速：10月攻克武汉，1927年3月占领上海、南京，共产党人组织的工农运动起了很大作用。然而国共联盟正在破裂。1927年4月12日，蒋介石在上海发动“清党”，镇压共产党人和工会，杀害多人，随即在南京另立国民政府；数月后武汉的国民党左派政府也宣布“分共”。

1928年蒋介石继续北伐。国民革命军逼近时，奉系军阀张作霖撤出北京，6月4日在皇姑屯被日本关东军军官预埋的炸药炸死。北京被攻克后改名北平。1928年12月29日，张作霖之子张学良宣布东北易帜，改挂国民政府旗帜。中国在南京国民政府之下实现了形式上的统一，但许多军阀仍拥兵自重。

summary.en: Japanese officers of the Kwantung Army blew up a section of railway near Mukden (Shenyang) and blamed Chinese troops, using it as pretext to occupy all of Manchuria within months.
summary.zh: 日本关东军炸毁沈阳柳条湖附近铁路并嫁祸中国军队，借机数月内侵占东北全境。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
Britannica: Mukden Incident

story.en:
Japan had held the South Manchuria Railway and the Kwantung Leased Territory since 1905, and many officers of its Kwantung Army believed Manchuria's resources were vital to Japan. Staff officers Ishiwara Kanji and Itagaki Seishirō planned to seize the region without waiting for Tokyo.

At about 10.20 p.m. on 18 September 1931 a small charge exploded beside the railway at Liutiaohu, just north of Mukden (Shenyang). The damage was so slight that a train passed over the spot minutes later. The Kwantung Army blamed Chinese soldiers, attacked the nearby Beidaying barracks and occupied Mukden by morning. The Chinese commander, Zhang Xueliang, ordered his troops not to resist, hoping for international intervention, and Japanese forces overran all three northeastern provinces within months.

In March 1932 Japan created the puppet state of Manchukuo with the last Qing emperor, Puyi, as its head. The League of Nations' Lytton Commission found Japan's action was not self-defence, and Japan left the League in 1933. Chinese historians often date the beginning of the War of Resistance to this night, and sirens sound in Shenyang every 18 September.
story.zh:
日本自1905年起控制南满铁路和关东州租借地，关东军中许多军官认为东北资源对日本生死攸关。参谋石原莞尔和板垣征四郎策划不待东京批准就武力夺取东北。

1931年9月18日晚十时许，沈阳北郊柳条湖附近的铁路旁响起一声爆炸。路轨损坏轻微，几分钟后便有列车照常驶过。关东军却诬称中国军队破坏铁路，随即进攻附近的北大营，次日清晨占领沈阳。东北军统帅张学良寄望于国际干预，命令部队不予抵抗，日军在数月间侵占东北三省全境。

1932年3月，日本扶植清朝末代皇帝溥仪建立伪满洲国。国际联盟派出的李顿调查团认定日本的行动并非自卫，日本于1933年退出国联。中国史学界常以这一夜作为抗日战争的开端，每年9月18日沈阳都会鸣响防空警报。

summary.en: Encircled in Jiangxi, the Red Army broke out and marched roughly 10,000 km through the southwest and northwest to Shaanxi. At the Zunyi Conference of January 1935 Mao Zedong gained leadership of the army.
summary.zh: 红军突破江西根据地包围，转战西南、西北约二万五千里抵达陕北；1935年1月遵义会议确立了毛泽东的领导地位。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
中共中央党史和文献研究院《中国共产党一百年大事记》
Britannica: Long March

story.en:
By 1934 the Nationalists' fifth encirclement campaign, using lines of blockhouses, was strangling the Communist base in Jiangxi. In October about 86,000 men of the Central Red Army broke out westwards, carrying presses, archives and machinery. Crossing the Xiang River in late 1934 cost them perhaps half their strength.

At Zunyi in Guizhou in January 1935 an enlarged Politburo meeting criticised the leadership of Bo Gu and the Comintern adviser Otto Braun, and Mao Zedong gained a leading role in military command. The army then manoeuvred across the Chishui River four times to shake off pursuit, crossed the Jinsha, and in May 1935 seized the chain bridge at Luding over the Dadu River. The heroic assault on the bridge became a founding legend; some historians think the fighting there was lighter than later accounts claim.

The marchers crossed snow-covered passes and the marshy Songpan grasslands, where many died, and split bitterly with Zhang Guotao's Fourth Front Army. In October 1935 fewer than 10,000 reached northern Shaanxi. The march preserved the party's core leadership and became a central story of its identity.
story.zh:
1934年，国民党第五次“围剿”以碉堡封锁步步推进，江西中央苏区岌岌可危。10月，中央红军约八万六千人携带印刷机、档案和机器向西突围。年底强渡湘江一役，红军兵力损失约半。

1935年1月在贵州遵义召开的中央政治局扩大会议，批评了博古和共产国际军事顾问李德的错误指挥，确立了毛泽东在军事指挥上的领导地位。此后红军四渡赤水摆脱追兵，巧渡金沙江，5月飞夺大渡河上的泸定桥。泸定桥之战成为红军的英雄传奇，但也有史家认为当时的战斗不如后来叙述的那样激烈。

红军翻越雪山、穿过松潘草地，沿途死伤甚众，又与张国焘领导的红四方面军发生严重分歧。1935年10月，不足万人抵达陕北。长征保存了中共的核心领导力量，并成为其身份认同的核心叙事。

label.en: Ruijin: the Central Red Army breaks out (Oct)
Crosses the Chishui River four times (Jan–Mar)
Crosses the Jinsha River at Jiaopingdu (May)
Seizes the Luding Bridge on the Dadu (May)
Meets the Fourth Front Army at Maogong (Jun)

label.zh: 陕北吴起镇：长征结束（10月）

summary.en: Generals Zhang Xueliang and Yang Hucheng detained Chiang Kai-shek at Xi'an to force him to stop fighting the Communists and resist Japan, paving the way for the Second United Front.
summary.zh: 张学良、杨虎城在西安扣押蒋介石，逼其停止“剿共”、联共抗日，促成第二次国共合作。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
Britannica: Xi'an Incident

story.en:
By late 1936 Chiang Kai-shek insisted on finishing off the Communists in northern Shaanxi before confronting Japan. The troops he assigned to the task, Zhang Xueliang's Northeastern Army, had lost their homeland to Japan in 1931 and had little will to fight fellow Chinese. Zhang and the Shaanxi commander Yang Hucheng had quietly opened contacts with the Communists.

Chiang flew to Xi'an to press them. Before dawn on 12 December, troops attacked his quarters at the Huaqing hot springs below Mount Li. Chiang fled in his nightclothes up the hillside and was found hiding in a crevice. The two generals demanded an end to the civil war, a united front against Japan and the reorganisation of the government.

The crisis was negotiated over the next two weeks, with Zhou Enlai representing the Communists and Song Meiling and T. V. Soong arriving from Nanjing. Chiang was released on 25 December without signing anything, and Zhang Xueliang flew back to Nanjing with him. Zhang was promptly tried and held under house arrest for over half a century; Yang Hucheng was killed in 1949. A Second United Front took shape in 1937.
story.zh:
1936年底，蒋介石坚持先消灭陕北的共产党，再对日作战。被派去“剿共”的张学良东北军在1931年失去家乡，无心与同胞作战。张学良与西北军将领杨虎城暗中与中共建立了联系。

蒋介石飞抵西安督战。12月12日凌晨，部队突袭他在骊山脚下华清池的住处。蒋介石穿着睡衣翻墙逃上山坡，后在一处石缝中被搜出。张、杨提出停止内战、联共抗日、改组政府等主张。

此后两周，危机通过谈判化解：周恩来代表中共参与斡旋，宋美龄、宋子文从南京赶来。12月25日蒋介石获释，未签署任何文件，张学良亲自陪同他飞回南京。张学良随即受审，此后被软禁长达半个多世纪；杨虎城则于1949年被杀害。1937年，第二次国共合作正式形成。

summary.en: A clash between Japanese and Chinese troops at the Lugou (Marco Polo) Bridge near Wanping, southwest of Beiping, escalated into the full-scale Second Sino-Japanese War.
summary.zh: 日军在北平西南宛平城、卢沟桥一带向中国守军开火，中国军队奋起抵抗，全面抗日战争爆发。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
Britannica: Marco Polo Bridge Incident

story.en:
By 1937 Japanese troops were stationed around Beiping under the Boxer Protocol and held positions on three sides of the city. Near Wanping, a walled town guarding the Lugou Bridge across the Yongding River, Chinese troops of Song Zheyuan's 29th Army faced Japanese units that held frequent night exercises.

On the night of 7 July 1937 a Japanese company reported shots fired and a soldier missing, and demanded to search Wanping. The soldier, Private Shimura Kikujirō, turned up soon afterwards, but the Japanese insisted on entry and fighting broke out at dawn. Local ceasefires were negotiated and broken while Tokyo sent reinforcements.

On 17 July Chiang Kai-shek declared at Lushan that China had reached the limit of its endurance and that "once war begins, every person has a duty to defend the nation." Beiping and Tianjin fell at the end of July, fighting spread to Shanghai in August, and Nanjing was captured in December. The incident began eight years of full-scale war that cost China, by most estimates, between 14 and 20 million dead or more.
story.zh:
到1937年，日军依据《辛丑条约》驻兵北平周边，已从三面包围北平。宛平城扼守永定河上的卢沟桥，宋哲元第二十九军的中国守军与时常进行夜间演习的日军对峙。

1937年7月7日夜，一个日军中队声称遭到射击、有一名士兵失踪，要求进入宛平城搜查。这名士兵志村菊次郎不久便自行归队，但日军仍坚持入城，次日拂晓双方交火。此后地方停战协议屡订屡破，东京则不断增兵。

7月17日，蒋介石在庐山发表谈话，宣告中国已到“最后关头”，“如果战端一开，那就是地无分南北，年无分老幼，无论何人，皆有守土抗战之责任”。7月底北平、天津相继失守，8月战火蔓延至上海，12月南京陷落。卢沟桥事变开启了八年全面抗战，据多数估计，中国死亡人数在一千四百万至两千万甚至更多。

summary.en: After Japan's surrender, the Japanese governor-general formally surrendered Taiwan and Penghu to the Republic of China in Taipei on 25 October 1945, ending fifty years of Japanese colonial rule.
summary.zh: 日本投降后，1945年10月25日台湾总督在台北向中华民国政府代表投降，结束日本五十年殖民统治。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
Britannica: Taiwan – History

summary.en: Centred on Xuzhou, the largest of the three great campaigns of the Chinese Civil War destroyed the main Nationalist field armies north of the Yangtze, after the Liaoshen campaign and alongside the Pingjin campaign.
summary.zh: 以徐州为中心，是解放战争三大战役中规模最大的一役，与辽沈、平津战役一起歼灭了国民党军主力。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
Britannica: Huai-Hai Campaign

story.en:
After the Communists won Manchuria in the Liaoshen campaign in the autumn of 1948, the Nationalists massed their main armies around the railway junction of Xuzhou to shield Nanjing. On 6 November the East China Field Army under Su Yu and Chen Yi and the Central Plains Field Army under Liu Bocheng and Deng Xiaoping opened a campaign on the plains north of the Huai River.

The Nationalist Seventh Army of Huang Baitao was encircled and destroyed at Nianzhuang in November, and Huang Wei's Twelfth Army, sent to relieve Xuzhou, was trapped and crushed at Shuangduiji in December. When Du Yuming tried to lead the Xuzhou garrison south, his forces were surrounded at Chenguanzhuang in heavy snow and annihilated on 10 January 1949; Du himself was captured.

About 555,000 Nationalist troops were killed, wounded, captured or defected. The Communist side mobilised several million civilian porters with wheelbarrows and carts; Chen Yi later remarked that the victory had been "pushed out by the people's wheelbarrows". With the Pingjin campaign ending in the surrender of Beiping the same month, the way across the Yangtze lay open, and Chiang Kai-shek stepped down as president on 21 January.
story.zh:
1948年秋，中共在辽沈战役中夺取东北后，国民党将主力集结于铁路枢纽徐州一带，屏障南京。11月6日，粟裕、陈毅指挥的华东野战军和刘伯承、邓小平指挥的中原野战军在淮河以北平原发起战役。

11月，黄百韬兵团在碾庄被围歼；12月，奉命增援徐州的黄维兵团在双堆集被包围歼灭。杜聿明率徐州守军南撤，在陈官庄一带被围，又遭大雪，1949年1月10日全军覆没，杜聿明本人被俘。

国民党军共约五十五万五千人被歼灭、俘虏或起义投诚。中共一方动员了数百万支前民工，以独轮车和大车运送粮弹；陈毅后来说，淮海战役的胜利“是人民群众用小车推出来的”。同月平津战役以北平和平解放告终，渡江的道路已经打开，1月21日蒋介石宣布“引退”。

name.en: Founding of the People's Republic of China

summary.en: Mao Zedong proclaimed the People's Republic of China from the Tiananmen rostrum in Beijing on 1 October 1949; the Nationalist government withdrew to Taiwan in December.
summary.zh: 1949年10月1日毛泽东在北京天安门城楼宣告中华人民共和国成立；同年12月国民政府迁往台湾。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
中共中央党史和文献研究院《中国共产党一百年大事记》
Britannica: China – Establishment of the People's Republic

story.en:
By the summer of 1949 Communist armies had crossed the Yangtze and taken Nanjing and Shanghai. In September the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference met in Beiping, which it renamed Beijing and made the capital. It adopted a provisional constitution, the five-star red flag and "March of the Volunteers" as the anthem, and elected Mao Zedong chairman of the Central People's Government. In his opening speech on 21 September Mao declared that the Chinese people "have stood up".

On the afternoon of 1 October 1949 Mao stood on the Tiananmen gate tower before a crowd of some 300,000 and announced that the Central People's Government had been established. He raised the new flag by pressing an electric switch, a 54-gun salute was fired, and troops paraded through the square.

Fighting continued in the south and west for months. On 7 December the Nationalist government moved to Taipei, beginning the division across the Taiwan Strait that persists. In the first decade the new state carried out land reform, joined the Korean War and adopted Soviet-style planning.
story.zh:
1949年夏，中共军队已渡过长江，攻占南京、上海。9月，中国人民政治协商会议第一届全体会议在北平召开，决定定都北平并改名北京，通过了起临时宪法作用的《共同纲领》，确定五星红旗为国旗、《义勇军进行曲》为代国歌，选举毛泽东为中央人民政府主席。9月21日，毛泽东在开幕词中宣告“中国人从此站立起来了”。

1949年10月1日下午，毛泽东在天安门城楼上面对约三十万群众宣告中央人民政府成立。他按动电钮升起第一面五星红旗，五十四门礼炮齐鸣二十八响，随后举行阅兵。

南方和西部的战事又持续了数月。12月7日国民政府迁往台北，海峡两岸由此分治至今。建国最初十年，新政权推行土地改革、参加朝鲜战争，并采用苏联式的计划经济。

summary.en: China detonated its first atomic bomb on a tower at the Lop Nur test site in Xinjiang, becoming the fifth nuclear power.
summary.zh: 中国第一颗原子弹在新疆罗布泊试验场铁塔上爆炸成功，成为第五个拥有核武器的国家。

summary.en: The Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in December 1978 shifted the party's focus to economic modernisation under Deng Xiaoping, leading to household farming, special economic zones and market reforms.
summary.zh: 1978年12月中共十一届三中全会把工作重心转向经济建设，邓小平主导下推行家庭联产承包、设立经济特区和市场化改革。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
《小岗村实行“大包干”回顾》《党史博览》2018年第7期 1978年12月 安徽凤阳县小岗村18户农民将集体土地承包到户，搞起“大包干”
中共中央党史和文献研究院《中国共产党一百年大事记》
Britannica: Deng Xiaoping

story.en:
Two years after Mao's death, the Communist Party's Central Committee met for its Third Plenum from 18 to 22 December 1978. Deng Xiaoping, rehabilitated the previous year, had prepared the ground with the slogan "seek truth from facts". The plenum ended mass class-struggle campaigns as the party's main task and made "socialist modernisation" its central goal.

Change in the countryside was already under way. A month earlier, eighteen farmers of Xiaogang village in Anhui had secretly signed a pact, pressed with their thumbprints, to divide collective land into family plots and to raise one another's children if they were jailed. Their harvest soared, and by the early 1980s the household responsibility system had replaced the people's communes nationwide.

In 1980 special economic zones were created at Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Shantou and Xiamen to attract foreign capital. Reform went on in fits and starts: prices were freed, state firms restructured, and after 1989 the pace slowed until Deng's southern tour of 1992 relaunched it. Over four decades China became the world's second-largest economy and hundreds of millions of people left extreme poverty.
story.zh:
毛泽东去世两年后，中共十一届三中全会于1978年12月18日至22日召开。前一年复出的邓小平以“实事求是”为口号为会议做了思想准备。全会停止使用“以阶级斗争为纲”的口号，把全党工作重点转移到社会主义现代化建设上来。

农村的变化其实已经开始。一个月前，安徽凤阳小岗村十八户农民秘密签订契约、按下红手印，将集体土地分包到户，并约定若有人因此坐牢，其余各户负责把他的孩子抚养到十八岁。次年粮食大幅增产，到80年代初，家庭联产承包责任制已在全国取代人民公社。

1980年，深圳、珠海、汕头、厦门设立经济特区以吸引外资。改革时进时退：价格逐步放开，国有企业改组，1989年后一度放缓，直至1992年邓小平南方谈话再度推动。四十年间，中国成为世界第二大经济体，数亿人摆脱了极端贫困。

summary.en: Under the 1984 Sino-British Joint Declaration, sovereignty over Hong Kong passed from the United Kingdom to the People's Republic of China at midnight on 1 July 1997, under "one country, two systems".
summary.zh: 根据1984年《中英联合声明》，1997年7月1日零时香港主权移交中华人民共和国，实行“一国两制”。

sources.title: Jiangshan Atlas 江山时序 (jiangshan-map, GPL-3.0)
Britannica: Hong Kong – History

story.en:
Britain held Hong Kong Island and Kowloon in perpetuity, but the New Territories, which made up most of the colony's land, were leased in 1898 for only 99 years. As 1997 approached, Margaret Thatcher hoped to extend British administration; Deng Xiaoping refused, insisting on sovereignty over the whole territory. Two years of talks produced the Sino-British Joint Declaration, signed by Thatcher and Premier Zhao Ziyang in Beijing on 19 December 1984.

China promised that under "one country, two systems" Hong Kong would keep its capitalist economy, common-law courts and way of life for fifty years, with a high degree of autonomy. These promises were written into the Basic Law of 1990. The last governor, Chris Patten, widened the franchise for the 1995 legislative elections, which Beijing rejected.

At midnight on 30 June 1997, in the new wing of the Convention and Exhibition Centre in Wan Chai, the Union Flag was lowered and the flag of the People's Republic raised before Prince Charles and President Jiang Zemin. Patten and the prince sailed away on the royal yacht Britannia in the rain. Tung Chee-hwa became the first chief executive of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
story.zh:
英国对香港岛和九龙半岛宣称永久占有，但占香港大部分土地的新界是1898年租借的，租期只有九十九年。1997年临近，撒切尔夫人希望延续英国管治，邓小平断然拒绝，坚持收回整个香港的主权。经过两年谈判，撒切尔夫人与国务院总理赵紫阳于1984年12月19日在北京签署《中英联合声明》。

中国承诺在“一国两制”下，香港保持原有的资本主义制度、普通法司法体系和生活方式五十年不变，实行高度自治。这些承诺载入1990年颁布的《基本法》。末任港督彭定康扩大了1995年立法局选举的选民基础，遭到北京反对。

1997年6月30日午夜，在湾仔会议展览中心新翼，英国国旗徐徐降下，中华人民共和国国旗升起，查尔斯王子与国家主席江泽民出席仪式。彭定康与王子随后冒雨登上皇家游艇“不列颠尼亚”号离去。董建华出任香港特别行政区首任行政长官。

summary.en: Beijing hosted the Games of the XXIX Olympiad from 8 to 24 August 2008, the first Summer Olympics held in China.
summary.zh: 第29届夏季奥林匹克运动会于2008年8月8日至24日在北京举行，是中国首次举办夏季奥运会。

name.en: Cai Lun presents paper to the Han court

summary.en: The eunuch official Cai Lun reported to Emperor He a method of making paper from tree bark, hemp waste, rags and old fishing nets. Paper fragments from earlier Han sites show the craft was older, but his cheap, standardised process spread writing paper across China and eventually the world.
summary.zh: 宦官蔡伦向汉和帝奏上以树皮、麻头、敝布和旧渔网造纸的方法。出土的西汉纸片表明造纸术早已有之，但他改进的廉价规范工艺使书写用纸在中国普及，并最终传遍世界。

sources.title: 范晔《后汉书》卷78 宦者列传·蔡伦
Britannica: Cai Lun
Wikipedia: Cai Lun

note: Hou Han shu dates the memorial to the first year of Yuanxing (105). No Wikidata item exists for the event; the QID is omitted rather than reusing Cai Lun's.

story.en:
Cai Lun entered the Eastern Han palace as a eunuch under Emperor Ming and rose under Emperor He to supervise the imperial workshops that made weapons and instruments. Writing at the time was done on bamboo slips, which were heavy, or on silk, which was costly. According to the Book of the Later Han, in 105 Cai Lun reported a new method of making paper from tree bark, hemp ends, old rags and fishing nets; the emperor praised it, and the material became known as "Marquis Cai's paper".

Archaeology shows that Cai Lun did not invent paper outright. Fragments of hemp paper from the Western Han, including one bearing a map at Fangmatan in Gansu, are more than two centuries older. His achievement was a cheaper, standard process using abundant raw materials that made paper practical for writing.

Cai Lun was made Marquis of Longting in 114, but he had been involved in palace intrigues, and when Emperor An took full power around 121 he took poison rather than face trial. Paper slowly replaced bamboo in China and spread to Korea, Japan and, by the eighth century, the Islamic world, eventually reaching Europe.
story.zh:
蔡伦在汉明帝时入宫为宦官，汉和帝时升任尚方令，主管制造兵器和御用器物的作坊。当时书写或用竹简，笨重不便；或用缣帛，价格昂贵。据《后汉书》记载，元兴元年（105年）蔡伦奏上用树皮、麻头、破布和旧渔网造纸的方法，和帝称赞其才能，天下咸称“蔡侯纸”。

考古发现表明，纸并非蔡伦凭空发明。西汉麻纸残片已多有出土，其中甘肃放马滩出土的一片还绘有地图，比蔡伦早两百多年。蔡伦的贡献在于用来源丰富的原料形成廉价、规范的工艺，使纸真正适于书写。

元初元年（114年），蔡伦被封为龙亭侯。但他曾卷入宫廷斗争，约121年汉安帝亲政后追究旧事，蔡伦不愿受审，服毒自尽。此后纸逐渐取代竹简，先后传入朝鲜、日本，八世纪传入伊斯兰世界，最终到达欧洲。

summary.en: According to a Tang inscription, the monk Lezun began cutting meditation caves into the cliffs near Dunhuang in 366. Over the next thousand years nearly 500 painted grottoes were added, making Mogao the largest treasury of Buddhist art on the Silk Road.
summary.zh: 据唐代碑记，366年僧人乐僔在敦煌附近崖壁上开凿禅窟。此后千年间陆续开凿近五百个彩绘洞窟，使莫高窟成为丝绸之路上规模最大的佛教艺术宝库。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Mogao Caves
Britannica: Mogao Caves
Wikipedia: Mogao Caves
UNESCO World Heritage: Mogao Caves

note: The date 366 comes from Li Huairang's stele of 698 (《李君莫高窟佛龛碑》); no caves that early have been securely identified.

story.en:
A stele of 698 preserved in the caves records the tradition of their founding. In 366 a wandering monk named Lezun, passing the cliffs of the Dang River valley southeast of Dunhuang at dusk, saw the opposite Sanwei mountain blaze with golden light like a thousand Buddhas, and cut a cell into the rock to meditate. Another monk, Faliang, followed, and local families began to sponsor caves as acts of merit.

Over the next thousand years, under the Northern dynasties, Sui, Tang, the Tibetan occupation, the Guiyi Army, the Western Xia and the Yuan, nearly 500 decorated caves were carved along 1.6 km of cliff. They hold about 45,000 square metres of murals and more than 2,000 painted clay statues, recording Buddhist scriptures and also daily life, music, dress and Silk Road trade.

In 1900 the Daoist caretaker Wang Yuanlu found a sealed side chamber, the Library Cave, packed with tens of thousands of manuscripts. Aurel Stein, Paul Pelliot and others bought large parts of it in 1907–08, so the collection is now split among London, Paris, St Petersburg and Beijing. Mogao became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987.
story.zh:
窟中保存的一通698年的石碑记载了莫高窟的开创传说：366年，云游僧人乐僔傍晚途经敦煌东南宕泉河谷的崖壁，忽见对面三危山上金光闪耀，状若千佛，于是在崖壁上凿窟禅修。其后法良禅师继至，当地世家大族也纷纷出资开窟以积功德。

此后一千年间，历经北朝、隋、唐、吐蕃统治、归义军、西夏直至元代，人们在长约一千六百米的崖面上开凿了近五百个彩绘洞窟，保存壁画约四万五千平方米、彩塑两千余身，不仅描绘佛经故事，也记录了当时的日常生活、音乐、服饰和丝路贸易。

1900年，看守石窟的道士王圆箓发现一间被封闭的耳室——藏经洞，其中堆满数万件写本文书。1907至1908年间，斯坦因、伯希和等人先后低价购走大批文物，如今这些藏品分散在伦敦、巴黎、圣彼得堡和北京等地。1987年，莫高窟被列入联合国教科文组织世界遗产名录。

summary.en: A woodblock-printed scroll of the Diamond Sutra, dedicated by one Wang Jie on behalf of his parents, carries the date 11 May 868. Sealed in the Library Cave at Mogao and found in 1900, it is the earliest complete printed book with a date; it is now in the British Library.
summary.zh: 一卷雕版印刷的《金刚经》由王玠为其父母敬造，题记为咸通九年四月十五日（868年5月11日）。它被封存于莫高窟藏经洞，1900年被发现，是现存最早有明确纪年的完整印本书籍，现藏大英图书馆。

sources.title: Britannica: Diamond Sutra
Frances Wood & Mark Barnard, The Diamond Sutra: The Story of the World's Earliest Dated Printed Book (2010)
Wikipedia: Diamond Sutra
British Library: The Diamond Sutra

note: Where it was printed is unknown; marker at the Mogao Library Cave (Cave 17), where it was found.

story.en:
The Diamond Sutra, a short Mahayana text on the emptiness of all things, was widely copied in Tang China because copying it was believed to earn merit. By the ninth century printers had learned to carve a whole page in reverse on a wooden block and press it onto paper, producing many copies at once.

The Dunhuang scroll is about five metres long, made of seven sheets pasted together. It opens with a finely cut frontispiece of the Buddha preaching to his elderly disciple Subhuti amid monks, guardians and donors. At the end a colophon states that Wang Jie had it made for free distribution on behalf of his two parents on the fifteenth day of the fourth month of the ninth year of Xiantong, which corresponds to 11 May 868. Nothing else is known about him.

The scroll lay sealed in the Library Cave at Mogao until 1900. Aurel Stein acquired it in 1907, and it is now in the British Library, which has digitised it. Older printed fragments exist, but it remains the earliest complete printed book bearing a date, and its skilled cutting shows that block printing was already a mature craft.
story.zh:
《金刚经》是一部阐述“一切法空”的大乘佛经，篇幅不长。唐人相信抄写此经可得功德，故而广为传抄。到九世纪，工匠已能将整版文字反刻在木板上，刷墨覆纸，一次印出多份。

这卷敦煌《金刚经》长约五米，由七张纸粘接而成。卷首是一幅刻工精细的扉画：佛陀坐于中央，向年迈的弟子须菩提说法，周围簇拥着僧众、护法和供养人。卷末题记写道：“咸通九年四月十五日王玠为二亲敬造普施”，即868年5月11日。关于王玠其人，别无记载。

此卷一直封存在莫高窟藏经洞，直到1900年。1907年斯坦因将其购得，现藏大英图书馆，并已全部数字化。虽然还有更早的印刷残片存世，但它仍是现存最早有明确纪年的完整印本书籍，其娴熟的刻工表明雕版印刷当时已是成熟的技艺。

summary.en: Written in retirement at his Mengxi garden in Runzhou (Zhenjiang), Shen Kuo's notebook records the magnetic needle compass and magnetic declination, Bi Sheng's movable clay type and ideas on land formation drawn from fossils. It is a key source for Song science and technology.
summary.zh: 沈括退居润州（今镇江）梦溪园时撰写的这部笔记，记载了磁针指南及磁偏角、毕昇的泥活字印刷术以及依据化石推断地貌变迁等内容，是研究宋代科学技术的重要史料。

sources.title: Britannica: Shen Kuo
沈括《梦溪笔谈》（维基文库）
Wikipedia: Dream Pool Essays

note: Written c. 1088 onward; Bi Sheng's movable type, which it describes, dates from the Qingli era (1041–1048).

story.en:
Shen Kuo was one of the most versatile officials of the Northern Song: an astronomer who reformed the calendar, a hydraulic engineer, a diplomat sent to the Liao and a military commander on the Xi Xia frontier. After a defeat at Yongle in 1082 for which he was blamed, he was demoted and eventually retired to an estate at Runzhou (Zhenjiang). He said he had dreamed of the place years before he bought it, and named it Mengxi, "Dream Brook".

There he wrote down, in more than 600 short entries, what he had seen and thought. He described a magnetised needle that "always points slightly east of south", the first known record of magnetic declination. He recorded how a commoner named Bi Sheng had printed with movable clay type in the 1040s, explained fossil shells in the Taihang cliffs as evidence of ancient shorelines, and described the shiyou ("rock oil") seeping from the ground in northern Shaanxi, predicting that it would one day be widely used.

The book also covers music, medicine, mathematics and court anecdotes. Joseph Needham called Shen Kuo perhaps the most interesting figure in Chinese scientific history, and the essays are a main source for Song technology.
story.zh:
沈括是北宋最为博学多才的官员之一：他是改革历法的天文学家、主持水利的工程专家，曾出使辽国，又在西夏边境统兵。1082年永乐城之败，他被追究责任而贬官，晚年退居润州（今镇江）的园宅。他说多年前曾梦见此地，买下后便命名为“梦溪”。

他在这里把平生见闻与思考写成六百余条札记。书中记载磁针“常微偏东，不全南也”，是世界上关于磁偏角的最早记录；记述了布衣毕昇在庆历年间以胶泥活字印书的方法；根据太行山崖壁中的螺蚌化石推断此处古为海滨；还记述了陕北鄜延一带地下渗出的“石油”，并预言“此物后必大行于世”。

此书还涉及音乐、医药、数学和朝野掌故。李约瑟称沈括或许是中国科学史上最引人入胜的人物，《梦溪笔谈》也是研究宋代科技最重要的史料之一。

summary.en: On the night of 23 January 1556 an earthquake centred near Huazhou in the Wei River valley devastated Shaanxi, Shanxi and Henan. Ming records put the dead at more than 830,000, many in collapsed loess cave dwellings, making it the deadliest earthquake on record.
summary.zh: 1556年1月23日夜，以渭河谷地华州附近为震中的大地震重创陕西、山西和河南。明代史料载死者逾83万，许多人死于黄土窑洞坍塌，这是有记载以来死亡人数最多的地震。

sources.title: Britannica: Shaanxi province earthquake of 1556
《明史》卷30 五行志三
Wikipedia: 1556 Shaanxi earthquake

note: Julian date; the Chinese date is the 12th day of the 12th month of Jiajing 34 (嘉靖三十四年十二月十二日).

story.en:
Late on the night of 23 January 1556, the twelfth day of the twelfth month of the 34th year of Jiajing, a great earthquake struck the lower Wei River valley around Huazhou, Weinan and Huayin. Modern estimates put its magnitude at about 8. Shaanxi, Shanxi and Henan were shaken, and damage was reported across a region hundreds of kilometres wide.

The death toll was so high because the valley and the surrounding loess plateau were densely settled and many families lived in cave dwellings dug into soft loess cliffs, which collapsed in the dark. Landslides blocked rivers, the ground split and spouted water and sand, and city walls fell. The Ming History records that more than 830,000 officials, soldiers and commoners died, a figure that cannot be checked but has never been surpassed for an earthquake.

A survivor, the scholar Qin Keda, wrote an account drawing lessons from the disaster. He observed that people who rushed outdoors were often killed by falling debris, and advised staying low inside until the shaking stopped, then leaving. He also noted that low houses of wood and bamboo survived better than heavy brick and earth buildings.
story.zh:
嘉靖三十四年十二月十二日（1556年1月23日）深夜，渭河下游华州、渭南、华阴一带发生特大地震，现代估计震级约为8级。陕西、山西、河南均有强烈震感，受灾范围方圆数百公里。

死亡人数如此之高，是因为关中平原及周边黄土高原人口稠密，许多人家住在依黄土崖壁开凿的窑洞中，深夜震时窑洞坍塌，人们无从逃生。山崩堵塞河流，地裂处涌出水沙，城墙也纷纷倒塌。《明史》记载“官吏、军民压死八十三万有奇”，这一数字虽无法核实，但至今仍是地震死亡人数之最。

幸存的学者秦可大撰文总结教训。他发现仓皇夺门而出者往往被坠落物砸死，因此主张骤遇地震时不要急于夺门而出，应在屋内静待，观察动静，震停后再相机外出。他还注意到木竹结构的低矮房屋比沉重的砖土建筑更能经受地震。

summary.en: Written while Song Yingxing was a county instructor at Fenyi in Jiangxi and printed in 1637, this illustrated encyclopedia describes farming, textiles, salt, ceramics, metallurgy, weapons and papermaking. Little circulated in Qing China, it was later valued in Japan and Europe as a record of Ming technology.
summary.zh: 宋应星任江西分宜县教谕期间撰成此书，1637年刊行。这部附有插图的百科全书记述了农业、纺织、制盐、陶瓷、冶金、兵器和造纸等工艺。该书在清代流传不广，后来在日本和欧洲作为明代技术的记录而受到重视。

sources.title: Britannica: Tiangong kaiwu
宋应星《天工开物》（维基文库）
Wikipedia: Tiangong Kaiwu

summary.en: After heavy winter snow and months of torrential rain, the Yangtze, Huai and Yellow rivers overflowed in summer 1931, flooding a vast area and leaving Wuhan under water for weeks. Estimates of deaths from drowning, famine and disease range from about 400,000 to several million.
summary.zh: 1930年冬季大雪及随后连月暴雨之后，长江、淮河和黄河于1931年夏相继泛滥，大片地区被淹，武汉城内积水数周。溺亡及随后的饥荒和疫病造成的死亡人数估计从约40万到数百万不等。

sources.title: Chris Courtney, The Nature of Disaster in China: The 1931 Yangzi River Flood (2018)
Wikipedia: 1931 China floods

note: Death tolls are highly uncertain: the 1932 University of Nanking survey gives about 150,000 drowned in the surveyed area; some estimates including famine and disease reach 3.7 million.

story.en:
The winter of 1930–31 brought heavy snow to central China, and the spring thaw was followed by unusually heavy rain. In July 1931 a series of cyclones dropped torrential rain over the Yangtze and Huai basins. The rivers rose above their dykes, and the Yellow River also flooded. Over the summer an area larger than England was submerged.

At Wuhan the Yangtze broke through the defences in August and the city stood under water for weeks; residents moved about by boat. On the night of 25 August the Grand Canal dyke near Gaoyou burst during a storm, drowning thousands of people in their sleep. Survivors crowded onto dykes and rooftops, where cholera, dysentery and hunger followed.

The Nationalist government set up a National Flood Relief Commission under T. V. Soong, which used foreign wheat loans to pay refugees to rebuild dykes. The aviator Charles Lindbergh and his wife Anne flew survey missions over the flood zone. Estimates of the dead vary widely: official counts were around 400,000, while some later estimates run to two million or more. Weeks later Japan's seizure of Manchuria began.
story.zh:
1930至1931年冬，华中地区降下大雪，春季融雪后又遭遇罕见的持续降雨。1931年7月，接连而来的气旋带来暴雨，长江和淮河流域水位漫过堤防，黄河也决口泛滥。整个夏季，被淹面积超过英格兰全境。

8月，长江洪水冲破武汉防线，城区积水长达数周，市民只能以船代步。8月25日夜，高邮附近的运河大堤在暴风雨中溃决，数千人在睡梦中被淹死。幸存者挤在堤坝和屋顶上，霍乱、痢疾和饥饿接踵而至。

国民政府成立救济水灾委员会，由宋子文主持，利用美国小麦借款以工代赈，组织灾民修复堤防。飞行家林德伯格和妻子安妮驾机在灾区上空进行勘察。死亡人数的估计差异很大：官方统计约四十万，后来也有估计高达二百万甚至更多。数周之后，日本便发动九一八事变侵占东北。

name.en: Wang Mang usurps the Han and founds Xin

summary.en: The regent Wang Mang accepted the throne from the child heir of the Western Han and proclaimed the Xin dynasty at Chang'an. His sweeping reforms of land, slavery and coinage failed, and after the Yellow River changed course the Red Eyebrows and other rebels rose against him.
summary.zh: 摄政王莽接受西汉幼主孺子婴禅让，在长安建立新朝。他推行王田、禁买卖奴婢、屡改币制等新政，均告失败；黄河改道后赤眉等起义四起，新朝迅速崩溃。

sources.title: 班固《汉书》卷99 王莽传
Britannica: Wang Mang
中文维基百科：新朝

story.en:
Wang Mang rose as a nephew of the dowager empress Wang Zhengjun, and he built a reputation for frugality and Confucian virtue while his relatives grew rich. When the Western Han emperors died young and childless, he governed as regent for the infant Ruzi Ying. Omens were produced on cue, among them a bronze casket said to contain Heaven's mandate, and in January of 9 CE he took the throne himself as emperor of Xin, 'New'.

He meant to rebuild the society described in the classics. All land was declared 'the king's fields' and could not be bought or sold; the trade in slaves was banned; state monopolies covered salt, iron and liquor; and the coinage was changed again and again until it was nearly worthless. Landlords resisted, and officials could not enforce the rules. Then, around 11 CE, the Yellow River burst its banks and moved its course, flooding the plain and driving starving peasants into bands such as the Red Eyebrows.

In 23 the rebels broke his army at Kunyang and stormed Chang'an. Wang Mang was killed in the palace and his head was sent to the rebel emperor. Later historians used him as the type of the hypocritical usurper.
story.zh:
王莽是太皇太后王政君的侄子，在亲族骄奢之时以俭朴、恭谨、尊儒博得声望。西汉末年几位皇帝早逝无嗣，他以摄政身份辅佐幼主孺子婴。符命祥瑞接连出现，其中有所谓"金匮图策"。公元9年正月，他索性登基，国号"新"。

王莽想按儒家经典重建理想社会：天下田地改称"王田"，不得买卖；禁止买卖奴婢；实行盐、铁、酒等"五均六筦"；币制一改再改，几成废物。豪强抵制，官吏无从执行。约公元11年黄河决口改道，泛滥华北平原，饥民纷纷聚为赤眉等武装。

23年，起义军在昆阳大破新军，随即攻入长安。王莽死于宫中渐台，首级被送往更始帝处。后世史家常以他作为伪善篡位者的典型。

summary.en: Eastern Han scholar-officials and Imperial Academy students who denounced the palace eunuchs were arrested and banned from office in 166; after a failed plot against the eunuchs in 168, a second purge in 169 killed Li Ying and many others, alienating the literati from the court.
summary.zh: 东汉士大夫与太学生抨击宦官专权，166年遭禁锢；168年窦武、陈蕃谋诛宦官失败，169年第二次党锢，李膺等百余人被杀，士人与朝廷离心。

sources.title: 范晔《后汉书》卷67 党锢列传
Cambridge History of China, vol. 1: The Ch'in and Han Empires (1986), ch. 5
中文维基百科：党锢之祸

name.en: Ban Chao restores Han power in the Western Regions

summary.en: Sent west with a small escort in 73, Ban Chao won over or subdued the oasis states of the Tarim Basin for three decades, became Protector General in 91 and sent his envoy Gan Ying towards Rome. He returned to Luoyang in 102 after his sister Ban Zhao petitioned for his recall.
summary.zh: 73年班超率三十余人出使西域，三十年间招抚或征服塔里木盆地诸国，91年任西域都护，97年派甘英出使大秦。妹妹班昭上书请求，他于102年回到洛阳。

label.zh: 伊吾（哈密）：随窦固击北匈奴

label.en: Shanshan: kills the Xiongnu envoys ('no tiger cub without entering the tiger's den')
label.zh: 鄯善：夜袭匈奴使者，"不入虎穴，焉得虎子"

label.en: Shule (Kashgar): his base for twenty years
label.zh: 疏勒：经营西域的根据地
焉耆：平定焉耆，五十余国内属
