summary.en: Tuoba Gui of the Northern Wei surprised the retreating Later Yan army of Murong Bao at Canhe Slope and massacred tens of thousands of prisoners. The defeat broke Later Yan and opened the North China plain to the Tuoba.
summary.zh: 北魏拓跋珪在参合陂突袭撤退的后燕慕容宝大军，坑杀降卒数万。后燕由此一蹶不振，拓跋氏得以进取中原。

sources.title: 魏收《魏书》卷2 太祖纪 登国十年
《资治通鉴》卷108 晋纪三十 太元二十年
中文维基百科：参合陂之战

note: The site of Canhe Slope is debated; most scholars place it near Daihai lake, Liangcheng county, Inner Mongolia, which is used here.

summary.en: Emperor Taiwu of Northern Wei took Guzang and ended the Northern Liang, the last of the Sixteen Kingdoms. After 135 years of division the north was under one dynasty, facing the Liu Song in the south: the start of the Northern and Southern dynasties.
summary.zh: 北魏太武帝攻克姑臧，灭北凉，十六国最后一国覆亡。北方经过一百多年分裂重归一统，与南方刘宋对峙，南北朝格局由此形成。

sources.title: 魏收《魏书》卷4上 世祖纪 太延五年
《资治通鉴》卷123 宋纪五 元嘉十六年
Britannica: Northern Wei dynasty

story.en:
Tuoba Tao, Emperor Taiwu, came to the throne in 423 and spent sixteen years campaigning. He took Tongwan, the white-walled capital of the Xia built by Helian Bobo, in 427, pushed the Rouran nomads back into the steppe, and in 436 drove the last Northern Yan ruler out of Longcheng.

The Northern Liang of the Juqu family still held the Hexi Corridor from Guzang, today's Wuwei. Its ruler Juqu Mujian was married to Taiwu's sister but had quietly kept up ties with the Liu Song in the south and with the Rouran. In 439 Taiwu marched west across the desert. His officials had warned that the land beyond the Yellow River was waterless, yet his army found pasture and snowmelt streams on the way. Guzang surrendered after a siege, and Mujian was taken east to the Wei capital at Pingcheng.

The conquest ended the age of the Sixteen Kingdoms. Some 30,000 households from Guzang, among them Buddhist monks and craftsmen, were moved to Pingcheng, and their skills helped shape the Yungang caves begun twenty years later.
story.zh:
北魏太武帝拓跋焘423年即位，此后连年征战：427年攻克赫连勃勃所筑的夏都统万城，又北击柔然，436年逼走北燕末主，取龙城。

此时河西走廊仍由沮渠氏北凉据守，都城姑臧即今武威。北凉国主沮渠牧犍娶太武帝之妹，却暗中与南朝刘宋及柔然往来。439年太武帝亲率大军西征。此前有大臣称河西之地缺水，不宜用兵，大军沿途却见水草丰美。姑臧被围后出降，牧犍被押往平城。

这次征服结束了十六国时代。北魏迁姑臧三万余户到平城，其中有不少僧人和工匠，他们的技艺影响了二十年后开凿的云冈石窟。

name.en: Carving of the Yungang Grottoes begins

summary.en: At the Northern Wei capital Pingcheng the monk Tanyao began five great cave-temples with colossal Buddhas, said to stand for the dynasty's first emperors. Over the next decades some 250 caves and 51,000 statues were cut, blending Gandharan, Central Asian and Chinese styles.
summary.zh: 北魏都城平城附近，沙门统昙曜主持开凿"昙曜五窟"，大佛据说象征北魏开国诸帝。此后数十年共凿洞窟二百余座、造像五万一千余尊，融合犍陀罗、中亚与中原艺术风格。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Yungang Grottoes
魏收《魏书》卷114 释老志
中文维基百科：云冈石窟

note: Tanyao's caves are usually dated to c. 460 (Heping era); the exact start year is not recorded.

name.en: Zu Chongzhi presents the Daming calendar

summary.en: The mathematician Zu Chongzhi submitted a new calendar to the Liu Song court that first took account of the precession of the equinoxes. He also bounded pi between 3.1415926 and 3.1415927, a precision not surpassed for about a thousand years. The calendar was adopted only in 510, under the Liang.
summary.zh: 数学家祖冲之向刘宋朝廷进献《大明历》，首次在历法中引入岁差。他还算出圆周率在3.1415926与3.1415927之间，这一精度保持了约一千年。该历直到510年梁朝时才颁行。

sources.title: 沈约《宋书》卷13 律历志下（祖冲之上表、戴法兴驳议）
魏徵等《隋书》卷16 律历志上（圆周率）
Britannica: Zu Chongzhi

summary.en: As Emperor Xiaowen moved the Northern Wei court to Luoyang, the Guyang cave was begun in the cliffs of the Yi River. Work continued for four centuries; its high point is the Tang Fengxian temple, whose great Vairocana was completed in 675 with funds from Empress Wu.
summary.zh: 北魏孝文帝迁都洛阳前后，伊河两岸开始开凿古阳洞。此后营造延续四百余年，以唐代奉先寺为巅峰，其卢舍那大佛于675年完工，武后曾捐助脂粉钱二万贯。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Longmen Grottoes
《河洛上都龙门之阳大卢舍那像龛记》（奉先寺题记，723年）
中文维基百科：龙门石窟

note: The Guyang cave is dated to around 493; the precise start is debated (493–495).

name.en: Sui conquest of Chen: China reunited

summary.en: Half a million Sui troops nominally led by Prince Yang Guang crossed the Yangtze; Han Qinhu and He Ruobi took Jiankang in early 589 and captured the last Chen ruler, Chen Shubao. China was reunited for the first time since the fall of Western Jin.
summary.zh: 隋以晋王杨广为元帅，发兵五十余万渡江；589年初韩擒虎、贺若弼攻入建康，俘陈后主陈叔宝。自西晋覆亡以来分裂近三百年的中国重归统一。

sources.title: 魏徵等《隋书》卷2 高祖纪下 开皇九年
《资治通鉴》卷177 隋纪一
Britannica: Sui dynasty

story.en:
Yang Jian had founded the Sui in the north in 581. For seven years he prepared: he built war fleets on the upper Yangtze in Sichuan and, according to the histories, had his troops change garrisons noisily along the river so often that the Chen defenders stopped taking alarm. In late 588 he sent more than half a million men under the overall command of his second son, Yang Guang, along a front from Sichuan to the sea.

The Chen ruler Chen Shubao was a poet who trusted the Yangtze to protect him. On New Year's Day of 589, while the Chen court feasted, He Ruobi crossed at Jingkou and Han Qinhu at Caishi. Within weeks Han Qinhu's horsemen entered Jiankang. Chen Shubao, the story goes, jumped into a palace well with two of his consorts; Sui soldiers threatened to drop stones and then hauled the three of them up together.

The Sui levelled the palaces of Jiankang, ending nearly three centuries in which it had been a capital of southern dynasties. North and south were joined under one government, and the Grand Canal soon tied them together.
story.zh:
杨坚581年在北方建隋，此后准备了七年：在长江上游的巴蜀造战船；据史书记载，他还让沿江驻军频繁换防、大张声势，久而久之，陈朝守军不再警觉。588年冬，隋以次子晋王杨广为行军元帅，五十余万大军从巴蜀到东海全线南下。

陈后主陈叔宝耽于诗酒，自恃长江天堑。589年正月初一，陈朝君臣正在朝会宴饮，贺若弼从京口、韩擒虎从采石相继渡江。不到一个月，韩擒虎率骑兵攻入建康。相传陈叔宝带着张贵妃、孔贵嫔躲进景阳殿旁的枯井，隋军扬言要往下扔石头，才把三人一起拉了上来。

隋军随后平毁建康宫室，这座南朝故都近三百年的繁华就此结束。南北重归一个政权统治，不久开凿的大运河又将两地连为一体。

summary.en: The Sui replaced recommendation by local notables with written examinations; under Emperor Yang the jinshi degree appeared. The Tang and Song made the exams the main road to office, and the system lasted until it was abolished in 1905.
summary.zh: 隋朝废除九品中正制，以考试选官，隋炀帝时始设进士科。唐宋以后科举成为入仕正途，一直延续到1905年废止。

sources.title: Britannica: Chinese civil service
杜佑《通典》卷14 选举二
Benjamin Elman, A Cultural History of Civil Examinations in Late Imperial China (2000)

note: The founding date is debated: Emperor Wen ordered prefectures to send candidates for examination in 587; the jinshi degree is traditionally dated to 605–607 under Emperor Yang.

story.en:
Under the Han and the Northern and Southern dynasties officials were chosen by recommendation, and from the third century by the Nine Ranks system, in which local assessors graded men largely by family. The saying went that the top grade held no poor families and the bottom grade no great clans. The Sui founder abolished the assessors, and under Emperor Yang a written examination for the jinshi degree appeared.

The Tang kept it but filled most posts by other routes. Wu Zetian, wary of the old aristocracy, widened the exams and is said to have questioned candidates in person. The Song turned the exams into a great machine: papers had their names covered and were recopied by clerks so that examiners could not recognise handwriting, and the cycle of prefectural, metropolitan and palace examinations was held every three years. Under the Ming and Qing the 'eight-legged essay' on the Four Books, read through Zhu Xi's commentaries, became the standard form.

For 1,300 years the examinations made classical learning the path to power. They were abolished by an edict of September 1905.
story.zh:
汉代与魏晋南北朝以察举、九品中正选官，中正官评定人才多看门第，以致"上品无寒门，下品无势族"。隋文帝废除中正，隋炀帝时出现了以考试取士的进士科。

唐代沿用科举，但多数官员仍出自其他途径。武则天为抑制旧门阀扩大科举，相传还亲自策问举人，开殿试先声。宋代科举制度臻于严密：试卷糊名、誊录，考官无从辨认笔迹；乡试、省试、殿试三级考试三年一举。明清以四书命题、以朱熹注释为准的八股文成为定式。

一千三百年间，科举使经学成为通向仕途的正途，直到1905年9月清廷下诏废止。

summary.en: A Tang army under Xue Rengui, sent to restore the Tuyuhun kingdom, was destroyed by the Tibetan general Gar Trinring Tsendro in the Qinghai highlands. The defeat left the Tibetan Empire master of the Kokonor region and opened a century of Tang–Tibet wars.
summary.zh: 唐将薛仁贵奉命护送吐谷浑复国，在青海高原大非川被吐蕃大论论钦陵击溃。吐蕃从此控制青海地区，唐蕃此后在西域、河陇争战百年。

sources.title: 刘昫等《旧唐书》卷83 薛仁贵传、卷196 吐蕃传
Christopher I. Beckwith, The Tibetan Empire in Central Asia (1987), ch. 2
中文维基百科：大非川之战

note: Dafei River is generally identified with the Qieji plain in Gonghe/Xinghai county, Qinghai; the point is approximate.

summary.en: Fleeing An Lushan's rebels, Emperor Xuanzong's guards mutinied at the Mawei post station west of Chang'an, killed the chief minister Yang Guozhong and forced the emperor to have Consort Yang Guifei put to death. Days later the crown prince left to take the throne as Emperor Suzong.
summary.zh: 唐玄宗西逃避安禄山叛军，禁军在长安以西的马嵬驿哗变，杀宰相杨国忠，逼玄宗赐死杨贵妃。不久太子北上灵武即位，是为唐肃宗。

sources.title: 《资治通鉴》卷218 唐纪三十四 至德元载
刘昫等《旧唐书》卷51 后妃传上 玄宗杨贵妃
中文维基百科：马嵬驿之变

summary.en: With Tang garrisons drained by the An Lushan rebellion, a Tibetan army swept through the Hexi region and took Chang'an in late 763, sending Emperor Daizong fleeing and enthroning a puppet. Guo Ziyi retook the city about two weeks later, but the Tibetans kept Hexi and Longyou for eighty years.
summary.zh: 安史之乱后唐边军内调，吐蕃大军乘虚东进，763年冬攻入长安，唐代宗出奔陕州，吐蕃另立傀儡皇帝。约半月后郭子仪收复长安，但河西、陇右被吐蕃占据长达八十年。

sources.title: 《资治通鉴》卷223 唐纪三十九 广德元年
Christopher I. Beckwith, The Tibetan Empire in Central Asia (1987), ch. 6
中文维基百科：吐蕃攻陷长安

name.en: Zhu Wen ends the Tang: the Five Dynasties begin

summary.en: Zhu Wen, a former Huang Chao rebel turned warlord, forced the last Tang emperor to abdicate at Bianzhou (Kaifeng) and founded the Later Liang. North China passed through five short dynasties while ten kingdoms divided the south.
summary.zh: 曾为黄巢部将的军阀朱温在汴州逼唐哀帝禅位，建立后梁。此后中原五个短命王朝相继更替，南方十国割据。

sources.title: 薛居正等《旧五代史》卷3 梁太祖纪
Britannica: Five Dynasties

story.en:
Zhu Wen had marched with Huang Chao, then defected to the Tang in 882 and was rewarded with the name Quanzhong, 'perfectly loyal', and the governorship of Bianzhou on the Grand Canal. Over twenty years he swallowed his neighbours and made the court his captive.

In 904 he forced Emperor Zhaozong to move from Chang'an to Luoyang. The palaces and houses of Chang'an were pulled down and their timbers floated down the Wei River; the greatest city of the age never recovered. Months later Zhaozong was murdered. In 905, at the White Horse post station on the Yellow River, Zhu's men killed some thirty senior courtiers. His adviser Li Zhen, who had failed the examinations, is recorded as saying that these men called themselves the 'pure stream' and should be thrown into the Yellow River to make them the 'muddy stream'.

In the spring of 907 the boy Emperor Ai abdicated, and Zhu Wen became emperor of Liang at Kaifeng. He was murdered by his own son in 912. The Tang's governors became kings, and China split for more than half a century.
story.zh:
朱温早年追随黄巢，882年降唐，被赐名"全忠"，任宣武节度使，坐镇运河要冲汴州。二十年间他吞并邻镇，把朝廷掌握在手中。

904年，他逼唐昭宗从长安迁都洛阳，拆毁长安宫室民居，木料顺渭河漂流东下，这座当时世界上最大的城市从此一蹶不振。数月后昭宗被弑。905年，朱温在黄河边的白马驿杀害朝臣三十余人，屡试不第的谋士李振说："此辈常自谓清流，宜投之黄河，使为浊流。"

907年春，唐哀帝禅位，朱温在开封称帝，国号梁。912年他被亲生儿子所杀。唐末藩镇纷纷称王，中国陷入半个多世纪的分裂。

name.zh: 耶律阿保机称帝建契丹国

summary.en: Yelü Abaoji, who had made himself supreme khan of the Khitan, took the title of emperor in 916, ending the tribes' custom of rotating leadership. He built Shangjing on the Xar Moron River, created a Khitan script and conquered the Balhae kingdom in 926; the state later took the dynastic name Liao.
summary.zh: 耶律阿保机统一契丹诸部后，于916年称帝，废除部落首领轮选制度。他在西拉木伦河流域营建上京临潢府，创制契丹文字，926年灭渤海国；国家后来定国号为"辽"。

sources.title: 脱脱等《辽史》卷1–2 太祖纪
Britannica: Abaoji
中文维基百科：耶律阿保机

summary.en: Fresh from conquering the Northern Han, Song Taizong besieged Liao-held Youzhou (Beijing), but Liao relief armies under Yelü Xiuge routed his forces by the Gaoliang River. The emperor escaped wounded, and the Sixteen Prefectures stayed in Khitan hands.
summary.zh: 宋太宗灭北汉后乘胜围攻辽南京幽州，在高梁河被耶律休哥等辽军援兵击溃，太宗负伤乘驴车南逃，燕云十六州终宋未能收复。

sources.title: 脱脱等《辽史》卷9 景宗纪、卷83 耶律休哥传
《续资治通鉴长编》卷20 太平兴国四年
中文维基百科：高梁河之战

summary.en: In the Qingli era a commoner named Bi Sheng carved characters in clay, fired them and set them in an iron frame with resin and wax, printing from two forms in turn. Shen Kuo's Dream Pool Essays is the only contemporary record of the world's first known movable type.
summary.zh: 北宋庆历年间，平民毕昇以胶泥刻字、火烧令坚，排于铁范内以松脂蜡和纸灰固定，两版交替印刷。沈括《梦溪笔谈》是这项世界最早活字印刷术的唯一同时代记载。

sources.title: 沈括《梦溪笔谈》卷18 技艺
Britannica: Bi Sheng
Joseph Needham & Tsien Tsuen-hsuin, Science and Civilisation in China, vol. 5.1: Paper and Printing (1985)

note: Shen Kuo dates the invention only to the Qingli era (1041–48) and does not say where Bi Sheng worked. The marker is Yingshan, Hubei, where a tombstone identified by some scholars as his was found in 1990; that identification is debated.

story.en:
Woodblock printing had been used in China for at least two centuries when, in the Qingli era of the 1040s, a man Shen Kuo calls simply 'Bi Sheng, a commoner' found a different way. He carved single characters on pieces of sticky clay as thin as a coin's rim and fired them hard. To print, he set them in an iron frame coated with pine resin, wax and paper ash, warmed the plate to soften the mixture, and pressed the type flat with a board.

Shen Kuo noticed the practical sense of it. Bi Sheng kept two frames, so that one was being printed while the other was being set; common characters such as zhi and ye were made in twenty or more copies; rare ones were carved on the spot. He did not use wood, Shen explains, because its grain swells with moisture. After Bi Sheng died his type passed to Shen's relatives, which is probably how Shen came to write about him.

For Chinese, with thousands of characters, woodblocks stayed cheaper for most books. But the idea spread: Wang Zhen made wooden type around 1300, and metal type was used in Korea by the thirteenth century.
story.zh:
雕版印刷在中国已流行至少两百年。北宋庆历年间，被沈括称为"布衣毕昇"的人另辟蹊径：用胶泥刻字，薄如钱唇，每字一印，用火烧硬。印刷时先在铁板上敷松脂、蜡和纸灰，把字排进铁范，加热使药剂稍熔，再用平板压平字面。

沈括记下了其中的巧思：毕昇备有两块铁板，一板印刷，一板排字，交替使用；"之""也"等常用字各备二十余个，生僻字则随时刻制。他不用木活字，是因为木纹疏密不一，沾水后高低不平。毕昇死后，他的泥活字为沈括的族人所得，这大概正是沈括得以记述此事的缘由。

汉字数以千计，对大多数书籍而言雕版仍更为经济。但活字的思路流传下来：约1300年王祯制造木活字，十三世纪高丽已使用金属活字。

name.en: Along the River During the Qingming Festival

summary.en: Zhang Zeduan's five-metre handscroll follows the Bian River from the countryside into the Northern Song capital Kaifeng, with more than 800 figures, boats, a rainbow bridge, shops and inns. It is the most detailed picture of a Chinese city before modern times and is now in the Palace Museum, Beijing.
summary.zh: 张择端的长卷沿汴河由郊野画入北宋都城东京，绘有八百余人、船只、虹桥、店铺和客栈，是近代以前描绘中国城市最详尽的图像，现藏北京故宫博物院。

sources.title: Britannica: Zhang Zeduan
张著跋（金大定二十六年，1186年），《清明上河图》卷后题跋
中文维基百科：清明上河图

note: The scroll is undated. The Jin colophon of 1186 is the earliest record; most scholars date it to the reign of Huizong (1101–1125), some to the late eleventh century.

summary.en: The Jurchen chieftain Aguda rebelled against his Khitan overlords in 1114, proclaimed himself emperor of Jin ('Gold') at Huining in 1115 and routed a far larger Liao army at Hubudagang. Within ten years the Jin had destroyed the Liao and turned on the Song.
summary.zh: 女真首领完颜阿骨打1114年起兵反辽，1115年在会宁称帝，国号"金"，同年在护步答冈以少胜多大败辽军。不到十年金灭辽，随即南下攻宋。

sources.title: 脱脱等《金史》卷2 太祖纪
Britannica: Jin dynasty
中文维基百科：完颜阿骨打

story.en:
The Jurchen of the Sungari forests sent the Liao court furs, pearls and gyrfalcons, and Khitan envoys who came to collect them were resented for their demands. In 1112 the Liao emperor Tianzuo held his spring fishing feast on the Sungari and ordered the tributary chiefs to dance. Aguda, a younger leader of the Wanyan clan, stood still and refused. Tianzuo thought of having him killed but was talked out of it.

Two years later Aguda rose with 2,500 men and took the Liao fort at Ningjiang. In 1115 he proclaimed himself emperor. The Jin shi records his explanation of the name: the Liao called themselves after fine iron, but iron rusts in the end, while gold does not change, and the Wanyan homeland on the Anchuhu River was named for gold. That winter Tianzuo marched against him with a huge army, and the Jurchen broke it at Hubudagang.

The Song, hoping to recover the Sixteen Prefectures, allied with the Jin in 1120. Aguda took the Liao capitals one by one before dying in 1123; under his brother Wuqimai the Jin captured Tianzuo in 1125 and then turned on the Song.
story.zh:
松花江流域的女真部落每年向辽进贡貂皮、北珠和海东青，前来索贡的辽朝使者常常勒索无度，女真人深为怨恨。1112年，辽天祚帝到春州混同江钓鱼，举行"头鱼宴"，命前来朝见的各部酋长依次起舞。完颜部的阿骨打"端立直视"，推辞不跳。天祚帝一度想杀他，被大臣劝止。

两年后阿骨打率两千五百人起兵，攻克辽宁江州。1115年他称帝。据《金史》记载，他解释国号说：辽以宾铁为号，取其坚固，但宾铁终会变坏，只有金不变不坏；完颜部又兴起于按出虎水，"按出虎"即女真语的"金"。当年冬天，天祚帝亲率大军来讨，在护步答冈被女真军击溃。

宋朝想借机收复燕云，1120年与金订立"海上之盟"。阿骨打相继攻下辽朝各京，1123年去世；其弟吴乞买在位时，金军于1125年俘获天祚帝，随即挥师南下攻宋。

summary.en: Yue Fei's cavalry defeated the Jin commander Wuzhu (Wanyan Zongbi) at Yancheng in Henan and again at Yingchang, bringing the Song armies near Kaifeng. The court, seeking peace, ordered him back, and the gains were abandoned.
summary.zh: 岳飞在河南郾城大败金兀术（完颜宗弼）的骑兵，继而再胜于颍昌，宋军逼近开封。朝廷一心议和，以十二道金字牌召回岳飞，所得之地尽弃。

sources.title: 脱脱等《宋史》卷365 岳飞传
李心传《建炎以来系年要录》卷136–137 绍兴十年
中文维基百科：郾城之战

note: Accounts of Wuzhu's armoured 'tuozi ma' cavalry come mainly from Yue Fei's grandson Yue Ke and are partly embellished.

summary.en: Genghis Khan raided the Tangut state from 1205, forced its submission in 1210, and returned in 1226 after the Tanguts refused troops for his western campaign. He died during the final siege in 1227; the capital Zhongxing surrendered soon after and its people were massacred.
summary.zh: 成吉思汗自1205年起屡攻西夏，1210年迫其称臣；因西夏拒绝出兵助其西征，1226年再度大举进攻。1227年成吉思汗死于军中，中兴府随即投降，城中军民遭屠戮。

sources.title: 宋濂等《元史》卷1 太祖纪
Ruth Dunnell, "The Hsi Hsia", Cambridge History of China, vol. 6 (1994)
Britannica: Xi Xia

story.en:
The Tangut Western Xia controlled the Ordos and the Hexi Corridor, a rich state with its own script, Buddhist canon and a capital at Zhongxing near modern Yinchuan. It was also the Mongols' nearest settled neighbour. Genghis Khan raided it in 1205 and 1207, and in 1209 he besieged Zhongxing and tried to flood it by damming the Yellow River; the dyke broke and flooded his own camp. The Tangut ruler still submitted and gave him a daughter in marriage.

When Genghis Khan asked for troops for his war against Khwarazm in 1219, the Tangut minister Asha Gambu is said to have replied that if he lacked soldiers he should not call himself khan. Genghis Khan remembered. In 1226 he returned, took the Hexi cities and besieged the capital. He died in August 1227 in the Liupan Mountains; the cause is uncertain, and the sources speak of illness or a fall from his horse.

The last Xia ruler surrendered and was killed, and the Mongols slaughtered much of the population, as the dead khan had ordered. The Tangut kingdom vanished so completely that its script was not deciphered until the twentieth century.
story.zh:
党项人建立的西夏占据河套与河西走廊，国力富庶，有本民族文字和西夏文大藏经，都城中兴府在今银川附近。它也是蒙古最近的农耕邻国。成吉思汗1205年、1207年两度攻掠西夏，1209年围中兴府，筑堤引黄河水灌城，堤坝溃决反淹蒙古军营。即便如此，西夏国主仍然称臣，献女和亲。

1219年成吉思汗征花剌子模，要求西夏出兵，西夏权臣阿沙敢不据说回答：既然兵力不足，又何必称汗。成吉思汗记下了这笔账。1226年他再度南下，攻占河西诸城，进围中兴府。1227年8月他死于六盘山一带，死因不明，史料有病逝、坠马等说法。

西夏末主出降后被杀，蒙古军按成吉思汗遗命大肆屠戮。西夏消亡得极为彻底，西夏文直到二十世纪才被重新释读。

name.en: Mongol conquest of the Dali kingdom

summary.en: To outflank the Southern Song, Möngke sent his brother Kublai on a long march through western Sichuan; his army crossed the Jinsha River on inflated skin rafts and took Dali at the end of 1253. The Duan kings were kept as hereditary governors, and Yunnan became a province of the Yuan in 1274.
summary.zh: 为迂回包抄南宋，蒙哥派其弟忽必烈经川西远征大理，大军以革囊渡过金沙江，1253年底攻下大理城。段氏被保留为世袭总管，1274年元朝设云南行省。

sources.title: 宋濂等《元史》卷4 世祖纪一
Morris Rossabi, Khubilai Khan: His Life and Times (1988), ch. 2
中文维基百科：蒙古灭大理之战

summary.en: Built on new instruments and observations from 27 stations across the Yuan empire, Guo Shoujing and Wang Xun's Shoushi calendar fixed the year at 365.2425 days. Taken over almost unchanged by the Ming, it was used for some 360 years.
summary.zh: 郭守敬、王恂等制作新仪器，在全国设二十七处观测点，编成《授时历》，定回归年长为365.2425日。明代《大统历》基本沿用，前后通行约三百六十年。

sources.title: 宋濂等《元史》卷52–55 历志
Britannica: Guo Shoujing
中文维基百科：授时历

summary.en: The Hongwu Emperor executed his chancellor Hu Weiyong for alleged treason, abolished the Secretariat and the office of chancellor, and ruled the ministries directly. Purges linked to the case went on until 1390 and are said to have claimed some 30,000 lives.
summary.zh: 明太祖以谋反罪处死丞相胡惟庸，随即废除中书省和丞相制度，由皇帝直接统领六部。此案株连持续到1390年，据称被杀者达三万余人。

sources.title: 张廷玉等《明史》卷308 奸臣传 胡惟庸
Britannica: Hongwu
中文维基百科：胡惟庸案

summary.en: After fourteen years of preparation and construction, the Yongle Emperor's palace in Beijing was finished in 1420: some 980 surviving buildings on a north–south axis behind a moat and wall. It was the seat of 24 Ming and Qing emperors and became the Palace Museum in 1925.
summary.zh: 永乐四年（1406年）开始备料营建，1420年北京宫城落成，中轴对称，四周环以城墙和护城河，现存建筑约980座。明清两代共有24位皇帝居此，1925年辟为故宫博物院。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Imperial Palaces of the Ming and Qing Dynasties in Beijing and Shenyang
Britannica: Forbidden City
《明太宗实录》卷232 永乐十八年十二月

name.en: The Ming rebuild the Great Wall

summary.en: After the Tumu disaster the Ming turned to fixed defences. Yu Zijun walled the Ordos frontier in 1474, and after Altan Khan reached Beijing in 1550 the walls north of the capital were rebuilt in brick and stone; Qi Jiguang added over a thousand hollow watchtowers. Most of the Great Wall seen today is Ming work.
summary.zh: 土木之变后明朝转向筑墙固守。1474年余子俊修筑延绥边墙；1550年俺答兵临北京后，京师以北的边墙改用砖石重修，戚继光又增建空心敌台一千余座。今日所见长城大多为明代所筑。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: The Great Wall
Arthur Waldron, The Great Wall of China: From History to Myth (1990)
张廷玉等《明史》卷178 余子俊传、卷212 戚继光传

note: Wall-building ran through most of the dynasty; 1474 (Yu Zijun) and c. 1600 bracket the main phases. The marker is Badaling, rebuilt in 1505 and later.

story.en:
Earlier dynasties had built walls of rammed earth across the north, but the early Ming relied on garrisons and campaigns into the steppe. The capture of the Zhengtong Emperor at Tumu in 1449 ended that confidence. In 1474 the governor Yu Zijun built a wall of about 1,770 li along the Ordos frontier with 40,000 conscripts in a few months, and border raids there fell away.

The great rebuilding came later. In 1550 Altan Khan's horsemen rode through a weak point and camped outside Beijing for days, burning the suburbs. The court began enclosing the capital's northern approaches in brick and stone. In 1568 Qi Jiguang, fresh from fighting the coastal pirates, was given command of the Jizhou sector. He found the old towers too small to shelter troops and built more than a thousand two-storey hollow towers, where soldiers could live and store arms; he even brought in men from Zhejiang to garrison them.

Badaling, Mutianyu and Jinshanling, the stretches visited today, all date from this period. The wall did not stop the Manchus, who entered China in 1644 when Wu Sangui opened Shanhai Pass.
story.zh:
前代多以夯土筑墙，明初则依靠边镇驻军和出塞征战。1449年土木之变明英宗被俘，这种自信随之破灭。1474年巡抚余子俊征发四万民夫，几个月内筑成延绥边墙一千七百余里，此后当地边患大减。

大规模重修是在后期。1550年（庚戌之变）俺答汗的骑兵从薄弱处突入，在北京城外驻扎多日，焚掠郊区。朝廷开始用砖石包砌京师北面的边墙。1568年，抗倭名将戚继光调任蓟镇总兵，他发现旧墩台过小，无法容兵，于是修建空心敌台一千余座，上下两层，可以驻兵、储存军械，还调来浙江兵驻守。

今日游人所到的八达岭、慕田峪、金山岭等段都是这一时期的遗存。不过长城并未挡住清军：1644年吴三桂打开山海关，清军由此入关。

summary.en: Under the Ming ban on private sea trade, smuggler fleets led mostly by Chinese merchants such as Wang Zhi, with Japanese and Portuguese partners, raided the Zhejiang and Fujian coasts. Hu Zongxian lured Wang Zhi to his death in 1559 and Qi Jiguang's drilled troops won at Taizhou in 1561; the trade ban was eased in 1567.
summary.zh: 明朝实行海禁，以汪直等中国海商为首、勾结日本人和葡萄牙人的走私武装侵扰浙闽沿海。胡宗宪诱杀汪直（1559年），戚继光以"戚家军"在台州九战九捷（1561年）；1567年隆庆开关，部分解除海禁。

sources.title: 张廷玉等《明史》卷205 胡宗宪传、卷212 戚继光传、卷322 日本传
Britannica: wakō
Kwan-wai So, Japanese Piracy in Ming China during the 16th Century (1975)

summary.en: Ming officials allowed Portuguese traders to settle on the Macau peninsula in return for an annual ground rent. Macau became the hub of the silk-for-silver trade between Guangzhou, Nagasaki and Manila and the gateway for Jesuit missionaries into China.
summary.zh: 明朝地方官允许葡萄牙商人居留澳门半岛，每年缴纳地租。澳门成为广州、长崎与马尼拉之间丝银贸易的枢纽，也是耶稣会士进入中国的门户。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Historic Centre of Macao
Britannica: Macau
中文维基百科：葡属澳门

note: 1557 is the conventional date; there was no formal cession, and Portuguese presence began a few years earlier.

summary.en: After decades of raids, the defection of Altan Khan's grandson in 1570 opened talks. In 1571 the Ming named Altan 'Shunyi Wang', the 'Obedient and Righteous Prince', and opened horse markets along the frontier; the northern border stayed largely at peace for decades.
summary.zh: 经过数十年战乱，1570年俺答之孙把汉那吉降明，双方开始议和。1571年明廷封俺答为顺义王，在边境开设马市互市，此后北部边境数十年基本安定。

sources.title: 张廷玉等《明史》卷327 鞑靼传
Britannica: Altan Khan
中文维基百科：俺答封贡

summary.en: The Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng, after a national land survey, extended across the empire a reform already tried in several provinces: land tax and labour service were combined and paid in silver. It reflected, and deepened, Ming dependence on silver from Japan and the Americas.
summary.zh: 内阁首辅张居正在全国清丈田亩之后，将各地已试行的一条鞭法推广全国：田赋与徭役合并，一律折银征收。这一改革反映并加深了明朝对日本与美洲白银的依赖。

sources.title: 张廷玉等《明史》卷78 食货志二 赋役
Ray Huang, Taxation and Governmental Finance in Sixteenth-Century Ming China (1974)
中文维基百科：一条鞭法

summary.en: After eighteen years working his way north from Macau, the Jesuit Matteo Ricci reached Beijing and presented the Wanli Emperor with chiming clocks and a clavichord. Allowed to stay, he published a world map and, with Xu Guangqi, a translation of Euclid, beginning the Jesuit presence at the Ming and Qing courts.
summary.zh: 耶稣会士利玛窦从澳门辗转北上十八年，终于抵达北京，向万历帝进献自鸣钟和西琴，获准留居。他刊行《坤舆万国全图》，与徐光启合译《几何原本》，开启了耶稣会士在明清宫廷的活动。

sources.title: Britannica: Matteo Ricci
R. Po-chia Hsia, A Jesuit in the Forbidden City: Matteo Ricci 1552–1610 (2010)
中文维基百科：利玛窦

summary.en: Qing troops under Prince Dodo stormed Yangzhou, defended by the Southern Ming minister Shi Kefa, and sacked it for about ten days. Shi Kefa was killed. Wang Xiuchu's eyewitness account made the massacre a lasting symbol of the Qing conquest; his figure of 800,000 dead is thought exaggerated.
summary.zh: 清豫亲王多铎攻破南明督师史可法坚守的扬州，屠城约十日，史可法殉难。王秀楚的亲历记《扬州十日记》使这场屠杀成为清军入关的长久记忆；文中八十余万的死亡数字被认为有所夸大。

sources.title: 王秀楚《扬州十日记》
张廷玉等《明史》卷274 史可法传
Lynn A. Struve, Voices from the Ming–Qing Cataclysm (1993)

note: The death toll is unknown; Wang Xiuchu's figure of over 800,000 comes from monks who cremated bodies and is considered inflated.

name.en: Battle of Penghu: Qing annexes Taiwan
name.zh: 澎湖海战与清朝统一台湾

summary.en: The Qing admiral Shi Lang, a former Zheng officer, destroyed the Tungning fleet under Liu Guoxuan off the Penghu islands. Zheng Keshuang, Koxinga's grandson, surrendered Taiwan, which the Qing made a prefecture of Fujian in 1684.
summary.zh: 原为郑氏部将的清朝水师提督施琅在澎湖海域大败刘国轩率领的明郑水师。郑成功之孙郑克塽献台投降，清廷于1684年设台湾府，隶属福建。

sources.title: 赵尔巽等《清史稿》卷260 施琅传
Tonio Andrade, How Taiwan Became Chinese (2008), ch. 11
中文维基百科：澎湖海战

story.en:
Shi Lang had been one of Koxinga's commanders until a quarrel in 1651, when Koxinga had his father and brother killed and Shi fled to the Qing. For years he urged an attack on Taiwan, and for years the court hesitated. After the Revolt of the Three Feudatories was crushed and Zheng Jing died in 1681, leaving a twelve-year-old heir and a divided court, the Kangxi Emperor gave Shi Lang command of the Fujian fleet.

In July 1683 he sailed for the Penghu islands, the stepping stone to Taiwan, with some 300 ships. Liu Guoxuan, the Zheng commander, had fortified the main harbour. After a first clash, Shi Lang regrouped his ships into small squadrons that attacked each enemy vessel together; most of the Zheng fleet was sunk or burned and Liu fled to Taiwan with a few boats.

Without a navy Tungning could not fight on. Zheng Keshuang shaved his head in the Manchu style and surrendered. At court some ministers proposed abandoning the island and bringing its people back to the mainland; Shi Lang argued that it shielded the southeast coast, and Kangxi agreed. In 1684 Taiwan became a prefecture of Fujian.
story.zh:
施琅原是郑成功部将，1651年二人反目，郑成功杀其父与弟，施琅投奔清朝。此后他多年力主攻台，朝廷却一再犹豫。三藩之乱平定，1681年郑经去世，继位的郑克塽年仅十二岁，郑氏内部纷争不已，康熙帝遂任命施琅为福建水师提督。

1683年7月，施琅率战船约三百艘进攻台湾的门户澎湖。郑军主将刘国轩在澎湖主港严密设防。首战不利后，施琅把战船编为小队，以数船合攻一船，郑军水师几乎全军覆没，刘国轩仅率少数船只逃回台湾。

失去水师的明郑已无力再战。郑克塽剃发降清。朝中有大臣主张弃守台湾、迁民回大陆，施琅上疏力陈台湾为东南屏障，不可放弃，康熙采纳其议。1684年清廷设台湾府，隶属福建省。

summary.en: The Kangxi Emperor led one of three Qing columns across the Gobi against the Dzungar ruler Galdan; Fiyanggū's western column caught and crushed Galdan's army at Jao Modo on the Tuul River. Galdan died the next year, and Khalkha Mongolia passed firmly under Qing rule.
summary.zh: 康熙帝亲率三路大军之一穿越戈壁征讨准噶尔首领噶尔丹，费扬古率西路军在土拉河畔的昭莫多大败噶尔丹。噶尔丹次年身亡，喀尔喀蒙古从此稳固归属清朝。

sources.title: 《清圣祖实录》卷173 康熙三十五年五月
Peter C. Perdue, China Marches West: The Qing Conquest of Central Eurasia (2005), ch. 5
中文维基百科：昭莫多之战

note: Jao Modo lies on the upper Tuul River southeast of Ulaanbaatar; the point is approximate.

summary.en: Rome ruled in 1704 and 1715 that Chinese Catholics could not honour Confucius or their ancestors with traditional rites, overturning the Jesuit approach. The Kangxi Emperor replied by restricting missionaries, and in 1742 the papacy closed the question; Christianity's growth in China stalled.
summary.zh: 罗马教廷于1704年和1715年裁定中国天主教徒不得行祭孔、祭祖等传统礼仪，否定了耶稣会的适应策略。康熙帝随即限制传教，1742年教廷再发禁令终结争论，天主教在华发展由此受挫。

sources.title: Britannica: Chinese Rites Controversy
D. E. Mungello (ed.), The Chinese Rites Controversy: Its History and Meaning (1994)
中文维基百科：中国礼仪之争

note: The dispute began in the 1640s (a 1645 decree of the Propaganda Fide); the record covers the decisive rulings of 1704–1742.

summary.en: Sectarian uprisings broke out in Hubei in 1796 and spread through the mountains of Sichuan and Shaanxi, with leaders such as the young widow Wang Cong'er. The Qing needed eight years, local militias and fortified villages to put them down, and the cost exposed the decay of the Banner armies.
summary.zh: 1796年白莲教在湖北起事，蔓延至川陕山区，首领中有青年寡妇王聪儿。清廷耗时八年，依靠团练和坚壁清野才将其镇压，巨额军费暴露了八旗、绿营的衰败。

sources.title: Britannica: White Lotus
赵尔巽等《清史稿》卷16 仁宗本纪
Philip A. Kuhn, Rebellion and Its Enemies in Late Imperial China (1970)

summary.en: After the Second Opium War, Prince Gong, Zeng Guofan, Li Hongzhang and Zuo Zongtang set out to 'learn the superior techniques of the barbarians': a foreign office, arsenals, shipyards, a translation college, steamship and mining companies and a modern navy. Defeat by Japan in 1895 showed its limits.
summary.zh: 第二次鸦片战争后，恭亲王奕訢与曾国藩、李鸿章、左宗棠等以"师夷长技以制夷"为宗旨，设立总理衙门，兴办军工厂、船政局、同文馆、轮船招商局和矿务，建立近代海军。1895年甲午战败暴露了其局限。

sources.title: Britannica: Self-Strengthening Movement
Cambridge History of China, vol. 10, ch. 10 (Ting-yee Kuo & Kwang-Ching Liu, "Self-strengthening")
中文维基百科：洋务运动

story.en:
In October 1860 British and French troops burned the Summer Palace while the Xianfeng Emperor sheltered in Rehe. His brother Prince Gong stayed behind to negotiate, and in January 1861 he set up the Zongli Yamen, China's first foreign office. The emperor died that summer, and Gong and the young Empress Dowager Cixi took power in the Xinyou coup.

The provincial generals who were crushing the Taiping had seen what Western guns could do. Zeng Guofan opened an arsenal at Anqing in 1861, where Chinese craftsmen built a small steamboat; Li Hongzhang founded the Jiangnan Arsenal in Shanghai in 1865; Zuo Zongtang began the Fuzhou Navy Yard in 1866. Later came the Tongwen Guan language college, the China Merchants Steam Navigation Company, the Kaiping mines and telegraph lines. From 1872 Yung Wing sent 120 boys, in four groups, to study in New England.

The movement was led by provincial officials with little central coordination, and it changed machines more than institutions. Funds for the navy were diverted, among other things to rebuild the Summer Palace. In 1894–95 Japan destroyed the Beiyang Fleet, and with it the hope that guns alone could save the dynasty.
story.zh:
1860年10月，英法联军火烧圆明园，咸丰帝避居热河。其弟恭亲王奕訢留京议和，1861年1月设立总理各国事务衙门，这是中国第一个外交机构。同年夏咸丰帝去世，奕訢与慈禧太后发动辛酉政变，掌握朝政。

镇压太平天国的地方大员亲眼见识了洋枪洋炮的威力。1861年曾国藩设安庆内军械所，中国工匠在此造出一艘小火轮；1865年李鸿章在上海创办江南制造总局；1866年左宗棠创设福州船政局。此后又陆续兴办京师同文馆、轮船招商局、开平矿务局和电报。1872年容闳率首批幼童赴美国新英格兰留学，四年间共派一百二十人。

洋务运动由地方督抚各自主持，缺乏中央统筹，改变的多是器物而非制度。海军经费屡被挪用，其中包括重修颐和园。1894至1895年，北洋舰队被日本歼灭，单靠船炮自强的希望随之破灭。

summary.en: After the Muslim revolts of the 1860s, Yaqub Beg had built a state in the Tarim Basin. Zuo Zongtang, arguing against those who wanted to abandon the far west, led Qing armies from Gansu, took Ürümqi in 1876 and the oases of the south by 1878. Xinjiang became a province in 1884.
summary.zh: 十九世纪六十年代回民起事后，阿古柏在塔里木盆地建立政权。左宗棠力驳"弃疆"之议，率军自甘肃西进，1876年收复乌鲁木齐，1878年平定南疆。1884年清廷设新疆省。

sources.title: 赵尔巽等《清史稿》卷412 左宗棠传
Hodong Kim, Holy War in China: The Muslim Rebellion and State in Chinese Central Asia, 1864–1877 (2004)
中文维基百科：左宗棠收复新疆

summary.en: War over Vietnam: in August 1884 the French fleet destroyed the Fujian squadron at Mawei in under an hour and attacked Taiwan, but in March 1885 Feng Zicai's troops won at Zhennan Pass. The Treaty of Tianjin nonetheless recognised France's protectorate over Vietnam.
summary.zh: 中法因越南问题开战：1884年8月法国舰队在马尾不到一小时内全歼福建水师，又进攻台湾；1885年3月冯子材在镇南关大捷。但同年《中法新约》仍承认法国对越南的保护权。

label.en: Tonkin: French and Black Flag Army clash
label.zh: 越南北圻：法军与黑旗军交战
马尾：福建水师覆没（8月23日）

label.en: Keelung and Tamsui: French landings in Taiwan
label.zh: 基隆、淡水：法军进攻台湾

sources.title: Britannica: Sino-French War
Lloyd Eastman, Throne and Mandarins: China's Search for a Policy during the Sino-French Controversy (1967)
中文维基百科：中法战争

note: Fighting in Tonkin began in 1883; open war between the two governments ran from August 1884 to April 1885.

summary.en: Inspired by Kang Youwei and Liang Qichao, the Guangxu Emperor issued over a hundred edicts on schools, the examinations, the army and government in 103 days. Empress Dowager Cixi ended it on 21 September, confined the emperor, and six reformers including Tan Sitong were executed; the Imperial University survived.
summary.zh: 光绪帝采纳康有为、梁启超的主张，103天内颁布上百道诏令，涉及学堂、科举、军队和官制。9月21日慈禧太后发动政变，幽禁光绪，谭嗣同等"戊戌六君子"被杀，只有京师大学堂得以保留。

sources.title: Britannica: Hundred Days of Reform
梁启超《戊戌政变记》（1898）
Luke S. K. Kwong, A Mosaic of the Hundred Days (1984)

story.en:
Defeat by Japan in 1895 shocked the empire's scholars. When the Treaty of Shimonoseki was announced, Kang Youwei, in Beijing for the metropolitan examination, drew up a memorial signed by hundreds of candidates urging reform. Over three years his study societies and Liang Qichao's journalism argued that China must change its institutions, as Meiji Japan and Peter the Great's Russia had done.

On 11 June 1898 the 27-year-old Guangxu Emperor declared that reform was state policy. Edicts followed one after another: modern schools in every province and an Imperial University in Beijing, an end to the eight-legged essay, new-style army training, the abolition of sinecure offices. Many officials simply did not act on them.

When the emperor dismissed senior ministers and brought young reformers into his secretariat, conservatives turned to Empress Dowager Cixi. On 21 September she resumed power and confined Guangxu on an island in the palace lakes. Kang and Liang escaped to Japan. Tan Sitong refused to flee, saying that no reform succeeds without blood, and he was beheaded at Caishikou with five others. Whether Yuan Shikai betrayed the reformers' plot remains debated.
story.zh:
1895年甲午战败震动士林。《马关条约》签订的消息传来，正在北京参加会试的康有为起草上书，数百名举人联署，要求变法图强，史称"公车上书"。此后三年，康有为组织学会，梁启超主笔报刊，鼓吹中国必须像明治日本和彼得大帝的俄国那样改革制度。

1898年6月11日，27岁的光绪帝颁布《明定国是诏》，宣布变法。诏令接连而下：各省设新式学堂，在北京创办京师大学堂，废八股，练新军，裁撤冗官闲职。但许多官员只是敷衍拖延。

光绪帝罢免守旧大臣、起用年轻维新派参与新政后，守旧派转而求助慈禧太后。9月21日慈禧重新训政，把光绪幽禁在中南海瀛台。康、梁逃往日本。谭嗣同拒绝出走，说"各国变法，无不从流血而成"，与另外五人在菜市口就义。袁世凯是否告密导致政变，史学界至今仍有争论。

summary.en: On the advice of Yuan Shikai, Zhang Zhidong and other governors, the Qing ended the 1,300-year-old examination system from the following year and promised degrees for graduates of new-style schools. A whole class lost its path to office, and many young men turned to study in Japan.
summary.zh: 应袁世凯、张之洞等督抚奏请，清廷下诏自次年起停止科举，新式学堂毕业生授予出身。延续一千三百年的选官制度就此终结，士人失去传统仕进之路，大批青年转赴日本留学。

sources.title: Britannica: Chinese civil service
《光绪朝东华录》光绪三十一年八月甲辰（立停科举以广学校谕）
中文维基百科：废除科举

name.zh: 中国抗日战争（全面抗战）

summary.en: From the Marco Polo Bridge clash in July 1937 China fought Japan for eight years, alone until 1941. The Nationalist government retreated to Chongqing while Communist guerrillas grew behind Japanese lines. Japan surrendered in Nanjing on 9 September 1945; Chinese deaths are estimated at 14–20 million or more.
summary.zh: 1937年7月卢沟桥事变后，中国进行了八年全面抗战，1941年前基本孤军奋战。国民政府西迁重庆，中共在敌后发展游击根据地。1945年9月9日日军在南京签署投降书；中国死亡人数估计在一千四百万至两千万以上。

label.zh: 重庆：战时陪都，屡遭轰炸

label.en: Hundred Regiments Offensive in north China
Japanese surrender signed in Nanjing (9 Sept)
label.zh: 南京：日军签署投降书（9月9日）

sources.title: Britannica: Second Sino-Japanese War
Rana Mitter, Forgotten Ally: China's World War II, 1937–1945 (2013)
中文维基百科：中国抗日战争

note: Chinese historiography also counts a fourteen-year war from the Mukden Incident of 1931. Casualty figures vary widely between sources.

story.en:
Japan had held Manchuria since 1931 and pressed into north China. When shots in the dark near the Marco Polo Bridge on 7 July 1937 escalated, Chiang Kai-shek decided to fight rather than concede again, and the Second United Front with the Communists, agreed after the Xi'an Incident, took effect. Chiang opened a second front at Shanghai in August, where his best divisions held for three months before the city fell; Nanjing followed in December, and the massacre there became the war's emblem of atrocity.

China traded space for time. Factories, universities and the government moved up the Yangtze to Chongqing, which Japanese bombers attacked repeatedly from 1938. Li Zongren won at Tai'erzhuang in April 1938; to slow the Japanese advance on Wuhan, Nationalist troops breached the Yellow River dykes at Huayuankou, a decision that drowned or displaced millions of civilians. Behind Japanese lines the Communist Eighth Route and New Fourth Armies grew from tens of thousands to around a million men.

After Pearl Harbor China became one of the Allies, and its seat on the UN Security Council reflected that. Japan surrendered in August 1945, and General Okamura Yasuji signed in Nanjing on 9 September. Within a year civil war resumed.
story.zh:
日本1931年占领东北，此后不断蚕食华北。1937年7月7日夜卢沟桥附近的枪声演变为冲突后，蒋介石决定不再退让，西安事变后形成的第二次国共合作正式实现。8月蒋介石在上海开辟第二战场，精锐部队苦战三个月后上海失守；12月南京陷落，南京大屠杀成为这场战争暴行的象征。

中国以空间换时间。工厂、大学和政府机关沿长江西迁重庆，1938年起重庆屡遭日机轰炸。1938年4月李宗仁指挥台儿庄大捷；为阻滞日军进攻武汉，国军在花园口扒开黄河大堤，数以百万计的平民因此溺亡或流离失所。在敌后，中共领导的八路军、新四军从数万人发展到约百万人。

珍珠港事件后中国成为同盟国一员，后来获得联合国安理会常任理事国席位也与此相关。1945年8月日本宣布投降，9月9日日军中国派遣军总司令冈村宁次在南京签署投降书。不到一年，内战再起。

summary.en: For three months some 700,000 Chinese troops, including Chiang Kai-shek's German-trained divisions, fought Japanese forces street by street in Shanghai and along the Yangtze shore. A landing at Hangzhou Bay outflanked them in November; the city fell, at the cost of perhaps 200,000 or more Chinese casualties.
summary.zh: 约七十万中国军队（包括德械师）与日军在上海市区和长江沿岸逐街血战三个月。11月日军在杭州湾登陆迂回，中国军队被迫撤退，上海失守，中方伤亡估计达二十万以上。

sources.title: Peter Harmsen, Shanghai 1937: Stalingrad on the Yangtze (2013)
Britannica: Second Sino-Japanese War
中文维基百科：淞沪会战

note: Casualty figures vary; Chinese losses are usually given as 180,000–300,000.

story.en:
After the Marco Polo Bridge clash, the fighting in the north went badly for China. Chiang Kai-shek chose to strike at Shanghai, where Japan had a marine garrison of a few thousand and where the world's press and the foreign concessions would watch. Fighting began on 13 August 1937. The next day Chinese aircraft trying to bomb the Japanese flagship Izumo hit the International Settlement by mistake, killing more than a thousand civilians.

Japan poured in divisions. Chinese troops, including the German-trained 87th and 88th, held Zhabei and the creeks around Luodian under naval bombardment and air attack; whole regiments were destroyed in days. A photograph of a burned baby crying amid the ruins of the South Station, taken on 28 August, went round the world. In late October, as the main army withdrew, about four hundred men of the 88th Division held the Sihang Warehouse on Suzhou Creek for four days in full view of the Settlement; a Girl Guide, Yang Huimin, is said to have swum the creek to bring them a flag.

On 5 November Japanese troops landed at Hangzhou Bay and threatened the Chinese rear. The retreat became a rout, and the road to Nanjing lay open.
story.zh:
卢沟桥事变后华北战局不利。蒋介石决定在上海主动出击：日本在沪仅有数千海军陆战队，而国际租界和各国记者都在这里注视。1937年8月13日战事爆发。次日中国空军轰炸日军旗舰"出云"号，误中公共租界，一千余名平民罹难。

日本不断增兵。中国军队包括德械第87、88师，在海军炮火和空袭下死守闸北和罗店一带的河网阵地，整团整团的部队在几天内拼光。8月28日一张婴儿在上海南站废墟中啼哭的照片传遍世界。10月下旬主力撤退时，第88师约四百名官兵（"八百壮士"）在苏州河畔的四行仓库坚守四天，租界居民隔河目睹；据说女童军杨惠敏泅渡苏州河为他们送去国旗。

11月5日日军在杭州湾登陆，威胁中国军队后方，撤退演变为溃退，通往南京的道路随之敞开。

summary.en: After capturing the Chinese capital on 13 December 1937, Japanese troops killed prisoners of war and civilians and raped tens of thousands of women over some six weeks. The postwar Tokyo tribunal put the dead at over 200,000; the Nanjing tribunal and the PRC give 300,000. A Western-run Safety Zone sheltered about 200,000 people.
summary.zh: 1937年12月13日日军攻占南京后，在约六周内大肆屠杀战俘和平民，强奸妇女数万人。战后远东国际军事法庭认定遇难者逾二十万，南京审判和中国官方认定为三十万以上。西方人士设立的安全区庇护了约二十万难民。

sources.title: Britannica: Nanjing Massacre
International Military Tribunal for the Far East, Judgment (1948), ch. 8
侵华日军南京大屠杀遇难同胞纪念馆

note: The death toll is debated among historians, with most estimates between about 100,000 and over 300,000; Japanese denialist claims are rejected by mainstream scholarship.

story.en:
Nanjing fell on 13 December 1937 after a chaotic retreat; the garrison commander Tang Shengzhi had promised to hold it to the death and then left. Tens of thousands of Chinese soldiers who had thrown away their uniforms were rounded up, along with men suspected of being soldiers, and shot, bayoneted or machine-gunned along the Yangtze banks. Japanese newspapers even reported a 'contest' between two officers to be the first to kill a hundred men with a sword.

For some six weeks troops looted, burned and killed across the city. Rape was so widespread that the foreign residents who stayed recorded thousands of cases. A group of about twenty Westerners, led by the German businessman and Nazi party member John Rabe, ran a Nanjing Safety Zone of about four square kilometres that sheltered some 200,000 refugees. The American missionary Minnie Vautrin turned Ginling College into a refuge for women. Their diaries and the film shot by John Magee are among the key sources.

After the war the Tokyo tribunal found that over 200,000 had been killed and hanged General Matsui Iwane; the Nanjing tribunal executed Tani Hisao. The massacre remains a deep wound in Sino-Japanese relations.
story.zh:
1937年12月13日，南京在混乱的撤退中陷落；卫戍司令唐生智曾誓言与城共存亡，最终却弃城而去。数万名脱下军装的中国士兵以及被怀疑当过兵的男子遭到搜捕，在长江边被枪杀、刺杀或集体机枪扫射。日本报纸甚至报道了两名军官"百人斩"竞赛。

在约六周时间里，日军在全城抢劫、纵火、杀戮，强奸案极为普遍，留在城中的外国人记录了数以千计的案例。以德国商人、纳粹党员约翰·拉贝为首的约二十名西方人士设立了面积约四平方公里的南京安全区，庇护了约二十万难民。美国传教士魏特琳把金陵女子文理学院辟为妇女难民所。他们的日记以及约翰·马吉拍摄的影片，是记录这场暴行的关键史料。

战后，远东国际军事法庭认定遇难者逾二十万，判处松井石根绞刑；南京审判处决了谷寿夫。南京大屠杀至今仍是中日关系中的深刻伤痕。

summary.en: Chinese armies under Li Zongren trapped two Japanese divisions advancing on the rail junction of Xuzhou, fighting house to house in the walled town of Tai'erzhuang on the Grand Canal. The Japanese withdrawal in early April 1938 was China's first major victory of the war and a great boost to morale.
summary.zh: 李宗仁指挥中国军队在大运河畔的台儿庄围击南下进攻徐州的日军两个师团，双方在城内逐屋争夺。1938年4月初日军撤退，这是全面抗战以来中国军队的第一次重大胜利，极大鼓舞了士气。

sources.title: Stephen MacKinnon, Wuhan 1938: War, Refugees, and the Making of Modern China (2008)
Rana Mitter, Forgotten Ally (2013), ch. 8
中文维基百科：台儿庄战役

summary.en: A clash between monopoly agents and a cigarette seller in Taipei set off island-wide protests against the corrupt postwar administration of Chen Yi. Troops sent from the mainland in March killed thousands, including many of Taiwan's educated elite; a 1992 government report estimated 18,000–28,000 deaths.
summary.zh: 台北专卖局查缉员与私烟摊贩冲突，引发全岛反对陈仪战后统治的抗争。3月从大陆增派的军队镇压，数千人被杀，其中有许多台湾知识精英；1992年行政院报告估计死亡人数为一万八千至两万八千人。

sources.title: Britannica: 228 Incident
行政院研究二二八事件小组《二二八事件研究报告》（1992）
中文维基百科：二二八事件

note: Death estimates range from a few thousand to about 28,000.

story.en:
When Taiwan returned to Chinese rule in 1945 many islanders welcomed it, but the administration of Governor-General Chen Yi soon disappointed them. Mainland officials held the top posts, state monopolies controlled trade, prices soared and rice was shipped to the civil-war mainland.

On the evening of 27 February 1947 agents of the Monopoly Bureau seized contraband cigarettes from a widow, Lin Jiang-mai, near the Tianma teahouse in Taipei and struck her with a pistol butt. A crowd gathered; an agent fired and killed a bystander. The next day protesters marched on the Monopoly Bureau and the governor's office, where guards opened fire. Within days protests spread across the island, and local leaders formed settlement committees that demanded reforms and autonomy.

Chen Yi negotiated while asking Nanjing for troops. The 21st Division landed at Keelung on 8 March, and soldiers shot their way through the cities. Lawyers, doctors, teachers, journalists and students were arrested and killed. The incident was a forbidden subject during the long period of martial law; President Lee Teng-hui apologised in 1995, and 28 February is now a memorial day in Taiwan.
story.zh:
1945年台湾光复，许多台湾人热烈欢迎，但行政长官陈仪的施政很快令人失望：要职多由外省官员担任，专卖制度垄断贸易，物价飞涨，大米又被运往内战中的大陆。

1947年2月27日傍晚，专卖局查缉员在台北天马茶房附近没收寡妇林江迈的私烟，并用枪托将她打伤。围观群众聚集，查缉员开枪误杀一名路人。次日民众游行至专卖局和长官公署请愿，卫兵开枪。几天之内抗议蔓延全岛，各地士绅组成"二二八事件处理委员会"，要求政治改革和地方自治。

陈仪一面谈判，一面向南京请兵。3月8日整编第21师在基隆登陆，军队一路开枪镇压，大批律师、医生、教师、记者和学生被捕杀害。在漫长的戒严时期，这一事件一直是禁忌话题；1995年李登辉总统代表政府公开道歉，如今2月28日是台湾的和平纪念日。

name.en: The Republic of China government moves to Taiwan

summary.en: As the Communists swept the mainland, the Nationalist government moved its capital to Taipei in December 1949, bringing gold reserves, the Palace Museum's treasures and perhaps 1–2 million soldiers and civilians. Chiang Kai-shek resumed the presidency in 1950, and the two sides of the Taiwan Strait have been governed separately ever since.
summary.zh: 中共军队席卷大陆，国民政府于1949年12月迁都台北，运去黄金储备和故宫文物，随迁军民约一百万至两百万人。1950年蒋介石复任总统，台湾海峡两岸从此分治。

sources.title: Britannica: Taiwan: History
Jay Taylor, The Generalissimo: Chiang Kai-shek and the Struggle for Modern China (2009), ch. 10–11
中文维基百科：中华民国政府迁台

story.en:
By early 1949 the Nationalists had lost Manchuria and the decisive Huaihai campaign, and Chiang Kai-shek stepped down as president in January, leaving Li Zongren to seek terms. Chiang kept control of the party and the army, and he had already begun moving assets to Taiwan: from late 1948 ships carried the central bank's gold and silver to the island, and the finest pieces from the Palace Museum collection, crated since the 1930s, were landed at Keelung.

The Communists crossed the Yangtze in April 1949 and took Nanjing and Shanghai. The government fled from Guangzhou to Chongqing and then Chengdu, and on 7 December the Executive Yuan decided to move to Taipei. Chiang flew out of Chengdu on 10 December. Over these years perhaps one to two million soldiers, officials and their families crossed to an island of about six million people.

On 1 March 1950 Chiang resumed the presidency in Taipei. An invasion seemed likely, but the Korean War broke out in June and the US Seventh Fleet was sent into the Taiwan Strait. The ROC kept China's UN seat until 1971; martial law imposed in May 1949 lasted until 1987.
story.zh:
到1949年初，国民党已失去东北，又在淮海战役中惨败，蒋介石于1月引退，由李宗仁代总统谋求和谈。但蒋仍掌握党和军队，并已着手将资产转移台湾：1948年底起，中央银行的黄金白银陆续船运至台，自三十年代起装箱南迁的故宫文物精华也在基隆上岸。

1949年4月解放军渡江，攻占南京、上海。国民政府从广州迁重庆，再迁成都，12月7日行政院决议迁设台北。12月10日蒋介石从成都飞往台湾。这几年间约有一百万至两百万军民、官员及家属渡海赴台，而当时台湾人口约六百万。

1950年3月1日蒋介石在台北复行视事。解放军攻台似乎迫在眉睫，但6月朝鲜战争爆发，美国第七舰队开进台湾海峡。中华民国保有联合国中国席位至1971年；1949年5月实施的戒严则一直延续到1987年。

summary.en: Imposed on 20 May 1949 and lifted only on 15 July 1987, martial law in Taiwan banned new parties and newspapers and underpinned the 'White Terror', in which tens of thousands were tried by military courts. Its end under Chiang Ching-kuo opened the way to democracy.
summary.zh: 台湾自1949年5月20日起实施戒严，直至1987年7月15日方才解除。其间党禁、报禁并行，数以万计的人在"白色恐怖"中遭军事审判。蒋经国晚年宣布解严，为民主化铺平了道路。

sources.title: Britannica: Taiwan: History
国家人权博物馆：白色恐怖历史
中文维基百科：臺灣省戒嚴令

summary.en: Mao Zedong's campaign to overtake Britain in steel and grain output merged farms into huge people's communes with public canteens and set millions to smelting iron in backyard furnaces. Inflated harvest reports and heavy grain procurement led to the Great Famine; critics such as Peng Dehuai were purged in 1959.
summary.zh: 毛泽东发动"大跃进"，提出"超英赶美"，把农村合并为规模庞大的人民公社，大办公共食堂，数千万人"大炼钢铁"。浮夸风导致高征购，酿成大饥荒；1959年庐山会议上提出批评的彭德怀遭到批判。

sources.title: Britannica: Great Leap Forward
Roderick MacFarquhar, The Origins of the Cultural Revolution, vol. 2: The Great Leap Forward 1958–1960 (1983)
中共中央《关于建国以来党的若干历史问题的决议》（1981）

note: The marker is Chayashan in Suiping county, Henan, the first people's commune (April 1958).

story.en:
In late 1957 Mao Zedong declared that China would overtake Britain in steel output within fifteen years. In 1958 the target shrank to a few years and then to one. In April farmers in Suiping county, Henan, merged their cooperatives into the Chayashan 'satellite' commune; by autumn nearly all rural China had been reorganised into some 26,000 communes, with private plots abolished and meals served free in public canteens.

Provinces competed to report miraculous harvests, and newspapers printed photographs of children standing on wheat said to be growing too thickly to bend. Peasants were pulled from the fields to build dams and to feed backyard furnaces with pots, tools and door hinges; most of the iron was unusable. Because procurement quotas were based on the false figures, the state took grain the villages did not have.

At the Lushan conference in July 1959 Defence Minister Peng Dehuai wrote Mao a private letter criticising the 'petty-bourgeois fanaticism'. Mao circulated it, denounced Peng, and launched a campaign against 'right opportunists' that silenced other doubters. The leap continued until 1960, when the famine forced retreat; the 1981 party resolution called it a serious error.
story.zh:
1957年底毛泽东提出十五年内钢产量赶超英国。1958年，期限缩短为几年，继而一年。4月，河南遂平县的农民合并合作社，成立"嵖岈山卫星人民公社"；到秋天，全国农村几乎全部改组为约两万六千个人民公社，取消自留地，公共食堂"吃饭不要钱"。

各省竞相虚报"高产卫星"，报纸刊登孩子站在稠密得压不弯的麦穗上的照片。农民被调离田地去修水库、建土高炉，把铁锅、农具乃至门环都投入炉中，炼出的铁大多无法使用。由于征购指标依据的是虚报的数字，国家从农村征走了农民根本没有的粮食。

1959年7月庐山会议上，国防部长彭德怀给毛泽东写信，批评"小资产阶级狂热性"。毛泽东将信印发与会者，批判彭德怀，随后开展"反右倾"运动，其他质疑者都噤若寒蝉。"大跃进"持续到1960年，饥荒迫使中央收缩调整；1981年的《历史决议》称之为严重错误。

summary.en: Caused mainly by the policies of the Great Leap Forward, compounded by bad weather, the famine of 1959–61 was the deadliest in recorded history. Estimates of excess deaths range from about 15 to 45 million, with most demographers near 30 million; Anhui, Sichuan, Gansu and Henan suffered worst.
summary.zh: 这场饥荒主要由"大跃进"政策造成，自然灾害加剧了灾情，是有记录以来死亡人数最多的饥荒。非正常死亡估计从约一千五百万到四千五百万不等，多数人口学者的估计接近三千万；安徽、四川、甘肃、河南受灾最重。

sources.title: Yang Jisheng 杨继绳《墓碑：中国六十年代大饥荒纪实》(2008)
Frank Dikötter, Mao's Great Famine (2010)
Britannica: Great Leap Forward

note: Death toll estimates differ widely by method (e.g. Ashton et al. 1984: c. 30 million; Yang Jisheng: c. 36 million; Dikötter: at least 45 million). The marker is Xinyang, Henan, scene of the worst local famine.

story.en:
By the winter of 1959 the communal canteens had run out of food in much of the countryside. Grain had been requisitioned on the basis of inflated harvest reports, much of it to feed the cities and to pay for Soviet loans and exports, and after the Lushan conference officials who reported hunger risked being labelled rightists. Peasants ate bark, grass roots and a kind of clay known as 'Guanyin earth'.

Xinyang prefecture in Henan became the most notorious case. Local leaders, determined to show they were not 'right deviationists', searched homes for hidden grain and beat those who resisted, while state granaries stayed locked. Internal party investigations later counted around a million deaths in the prefecture. Similar disasters struck Anhui, Sichuan, Guizhou and Gansu.

In 1961 Liu Shaoqi visited his home village in Hunan and concluded that the famine was largely man-made. At the 'Seven Thousand Cadres' conference in January 1962 he said so in public, and the communes were scaled back, canteens closed and private plots restored. The famine was hidden from the world at the time; demographers working from the 1982 census later estimated roughly thirty million excess deaths.
story.zh:
到1959年冬，许多农村的公共食堂已经断粮。粮食征购依据的是浮夸的产量，大量粮食被运往城市、用于偿还苏联债务和出口；庐山会议后，报告饥荒的干部有被扣上"右倾"帽子的危险。农民以树皮、草根和一种叫"观音土"的黏土充饥。

河南信阳地区是最惨烈的例子。当地领导为表明自己不是"右倾"，挨家挨户搜查"瞒产私分"的粮食，殴打反抗者，国家粮库却紧闭不开。后来党内调查统计，该地区死亡人数约一百万。安徽、四川、贵州、甘肃等地也发生了类似惨剧。

1961年，刘少奇回到湖南老家调查，认为饥荒主要是人祸。1962年1月"七千人大会"上，他公开表达了这一看法；此后人民公社规模缩小，公共食堂解散，自留地恢复。当时饥荒对外严密封锁；人口学家后来根据1982年人口普查数据，估计非正常死亡约三千万人。

summary.en: Mao Zedong launched the 'Great Proletarian Cultural Revolution' in 1966 against alleged revisionists in the party. Red Guards attacked teachers, officials and cultural relics; President Liu Shaoqi died in detention. It ended with Mao's death and the arrest of the Gang of Four in 1976; deaths are estimated at one to two million or more.
summary.zh: 1966年毛泽东发动"无产阶级文化大革命"，矛头指向党内所谓"走资本主义道路的当权派"。红卫兵批斗教师和干部，破坏文物；国家主席刘少奇被迫害致死。1976年毛泽东去世、"四人帮"被捕，运动结束；死亡人数估计在一百万至两百万以上。

sources.title: Britannica: Cultural Revolution
Roderick MacFarquhar & Michael Schoenhals, Mao's Last Revolution (2006)
中共中央《关于建国以来党的若干历史问题的决议》（1981）

note: Casualty estimates vary widely; MacFarquhar and Schoenhals cite 750,000–1.5 million deaths in rural China alone.

story.en:
After the Great Leap, Liu Shaoqi and Deng Xiaoping had steered the economy back to recovery, and Mao Zedong came to fear that the party was sliding towards Soviet-style 'revisionism'. In May 1966 the Politburo issued a notice against 'representatives of the bourgeoisie' inside the party. On 18 August Mao, wearing army uniform, reviewed a million students on Tiananmen Square, and Red Guard units spread across the country.

They attacked the 'Four Olds' (old customs, culture, habits and ideas), ransacked temples and libraries, and humiliated and beat teachers and officials at 'struggle sessions'. The writer Lao She drowned himself in 1966 after being beaten. Liu Shaoqi was expelled from the party and died in 1969, untreated and under a false name, in Kaifeng; Deng Xiaoping was sent to work in a tractor factory in Jiangxi. Factional fighting brought the country close to civil war, and from 1968 some 17 million urban youths were 'sent down' to the countryside.

Mao's chosen successor Lin Biao died in a plane crash in Mongolia in 1971 after an apparent coup plot. Mao died in September 1976; a month later the Gang of Four, led by his widow Jiang Qing, was arrested. The party later called the decade a catastrophe.
story.zh:
"大跃进"后，刘少奇、邓小平主持经济调整，国民经济逐步恢复，毛泽东却担心党会滑向苏联式的"修正主义"。1966年5月，中央政治局通过《五一六通知》，矛头指向"混进党里的资产阶级代表人物"。8月18日，身着军装的毛泽东在天安门广场接见百万学生，红卫兵运动迅速席卷全国。

红卫兵"破四旧"（旧思想、旧文化、旧风俗、旧习惯），捣毁寺庙和图书馆，在批斗会上羞辱、殴打教师和干部。作家老舍1966年遭批斗毒打后投湖自尽。刘少奇被开除党籍，1969年在开封被化名关押，因得不到治疗而死；邓小平被下放到江西一家拖拉机修造厂劳动。派系武斗使国家濒临内战，1968年起约一千七百万城市青年"上山下乡"。

1971年，毛泽东钦定的接班人林彪在疑似政变阴谋败露后乘机外逃，坠毁于蒙古。1976年9月毛泽东去世，一个月后以其遗孀江青为首的"四人帮"被逮捕。中共后来称这十年为一场"浩劫"。

summary.en: A magnitude 7.6–7.8 earthquake struck the coal-mining city of Tangshan at 3:42 am, flattening most of its buildings while people slept. The official toll was 242,769 dead; some estimates are higher. The government declined foreign aid, and the disaster came weeks before Mao's death.
summary.zh: 凌晨3时42分，唐山发生7.8级（一说7.6级）大地震，这座煤矿城市的建筑在人们熟睡中几乎全部倒塌。官方公布死亡242,769人，一些估计更高。中国政府婉拒国际援助；一个多月后毛泽东去世。

sources.title: Britannica: Tangshan earthquake of 1976
USGS: Historic Earthquakes – Tangshan, China 1976
中文维基百科：唐山大地震

note: Chinese sources give magnitude 7.8 (surface-wave); the USGS gives Mw 7.5–7.6.

story.en:
Tangshan, 150 km east of Beijing, was an industrial city of about a million people, built on coal mines and almost entirely of unreinforced brick. At 3:42 on the morning of 28 July 1976 a fault ran directly beneath it. In about twenty seconds some 85 per cent of its buildings collapsed. A strong aftershock that evening brought down much of what was left.

Roads and bridges were broken and communications cut; the first report reached Beijing when a mine official drove there through the night. More than 100,000 soldiers were sent in, many digging with their hands. Most of the miners working underground at the Kailuan mines climbed out alive. The government declined offers of foreign help, and for years it released no casualty figures; the official count of 242,769 dead was published only in 1979.

The year had already seen the deaths of Zhou Enlai in January and Zhu De in early July. To many Chinese, steeped in the old idea that natural disasters signal the end of a mandate, the earthquake was an omen; Mao Zedong died on 9 September. Tangshan was rebuilt on the same site, and survivors' stories later inspired the film Aftershock (2010).
story.zh:
唐山位于北京以东约一百五十公里，是一座约百万人口的工业城市，依煤矿而兴，房屋几乎全是无钢筋的砖结构。1976年7月28日凌晨3时42分，断层恰好在城市正下方破裂，约二十秒内全市约百分之八十五的建筑倒塌。当晚一次强余震又震塌了大部分残存建筑。

道路桥梁断裂，通讯中断，第一份灾情报告是开滦煤矿的一名干部连夜驱车赶到北京送达的。十余万解放军官兵奉命救灾，许多人徒手挖掘。开滦煤矿井下的矿工大多自行爬出矿井，幸免于难。中国政府婉拒外国援助，多年未公布伤亡数字，直到1979年才公布死亡242,769人。

这一年1月周恩来去世，7月初朱德去世。在"天灾示警、天命将移"的传统观念中，许多中国人把地震视为不祥之兆；9月9日毛泽东逝世。唐山在原址重建，幸存者的故事后来被拍成电影《唐山大地震》（2010）。

summary.en: Mourning for the reformist leader Hu Yaobang grew into weeks of student-led protests and hunger strikes in Tiananmen Square, joined by workers and spreading to many cities. After martial law was declared, the army cleared Beijing on the night of 3–4 June, killing hundreds or more; party leader Zhao Ziyang was purged.
summary.zh: 悼念改革派领导人胡耀邦的活动演变为以学生为主、在天安门广场持续数周的抗议和绝食，工人和市民加入，并蔓延到多座城市。宣布戒严后，军队于6月3日夜至4日清场，造成数百人以上死亡；中共中央总书记赵紫阳被撤职。

sources.title: Britannica: Tiananmen Square incident
Andrew Nathan & Perry Link (eds.), The Tiananmen Papers (2001)
Louisa Lim, The People's Republic of Amnesia (2014)

note: The death toll is unknown; the Chinese government reported about 200–300 dead including soldiers, while other estimates range from several hundred to several thousand.

story.en:
Hu Yaobang, the party general secretary dismissed in 1987 for being too tolerant of student demands, died of a heart attack on 15 April 1989. Students in Beijing laid wreaths at the Monument to the People's Heroes, and the mourning became a movement against corruption and inflation and for press freedom and dialogue with the leadership. A People's Daily editorial of 26 April calling it 'turmoil' angered them further.

On 13 May some students began a hunger strike in Tiananmen Square, days before Mikhail Gorbachev's state visit, the first Sino-Soviet summit in thirty years; the welcoming ceremony had to be moved. At the peak perhaps a million people filled central Beijing, and protests spread to many cities. On 19 May Zhao Ziyang visited the hunger strikers and told them, 'We came too late.' He was soon stripped of power, and martial law was declared on 20 May.

On the night of 3–4 June troops forced their way into the city along Chang'an Avenue, firing on crowds, and cleared the square by dawn. The death toll has never been established. On 5 June an unknown man stood in front of a column of tanks. The government called its action necessary for stability; the subject remains censored in the PRC.
story.zh:
1987年因对学潮态度宽容而被迫辞职的前中共中央总书记胡耀邦，于1989年4月15日因心脏病去世。北京学生到人民英雄纪念碑前献花圈，悼念活动演变为反对腐败和通货膨胀、要求新闻自由和与领导层对话的运动。4月26日《人民日报》社论将其定性为"动乱"，令学生更加愤慨。

5月13日，部分学生在天安门广场开始绝食，几天后戈尔巴乔夫来访，这是三十年来首次中苏首脑会晤，欢迎仪式被迫改换地点。高峰时北京市中心聚集了约百万人，抗议蔓延到许多城市。5月19日赵紫阳到广场探望绝食学生，说："我们来得太晚了。"他随即被解除职务，5月20日北京宣布戒严。

6月3日夜至4日，军队沿长安街强行进城，向人群开枪，黎明前完成清场。死亡人数至今没有定论。6月5日，一名身份不明的男子只身挡在坦克车队前。中国政府称此举是维护稳定所必需；在中华人民共和国境内，这一话题至今仍受审查。

summary.en: First proposed by Sun Yat-sen, the dam across the Yangtze at Sandouping was begun in 1994 and its main wall completed in 2006. The world's largest hydroelectric plant, with 22.5 GW capacity, it also controls floods, but its reservoir displaced about 1.3 million people and drowned towns and archaeological sites.
summary.zh: 孙中山最早提出构想，三峡大坝于1994年在长江三斗坪动工，2006年坝体全线建成。它是世界装机容量最大的水电站（2250万千瓦），兼具防洪功能，但水库淹没城镇和古迹，移民约一百三十万人。

summary.en: Under the Sino-Portuguese Joint Declaration of 1987, Portugal returned Macau to China at midnight on 20 December 1999, ending some 440 years of Portuguese presence. It became a Special Administrative Region under 'one country, two systems', and its casino economy later outgrew Las Vegas.
summary.zh: 根据1987年《中葡联合声明》，葡萄牙于1999年12月20日零时将澳门交还中国，结束了约四百四十年的葡萄牙管治。澳门成为实行"一国两制"的特别行政区，其博彩业后来规模超过拉斯维加斯。

name.en: China joins the World Trade Organization
name.zh: 中国加入世界贸易组织

summary.en: After fifteen years of negotiation, China became the WTO's 143rd member, cutting tariffs and opening services in return for permanent access to world markets. Exports multiplied over the next decade, and by 2009 China was the world's largest exporter.
summary.zh: 经过十五年谈判，中国成为世界贸易组织第143个成员，承诺降低关税、开放服务业，换取稳定进入世界市场的机会。此后十年出口成倍增长，2009年中国成为世界第一大出口国。

sources.title: WTO: China and the WTO (member information)
Nicholas Lardy, Integrating China into the Global Economy (2002)
中文维基百科：中国加入世界贸易组织

story.en:
China applied in 1986 to resume its seat in GATT, which the Republic of China had left in 1950. The talks dragged on through the Tiananmen crisis, the founding of the WTO in 1995 and bitter bargaining with the United States and the European Union over farm subsidies, banking, telecoms and car tariffs. Premier Zhu Rongji pushed the deal through against resistance from state industries, and the chief negotiator Long Yongtu later joked that his hair had turned white over the years of talks.

The decisive US–China agreement was signed in Beijing in November 1999. On 10 November 2001, at the ministerial conference in Doha, members approved China's accession, and it took effect on 11 December; Taiwan joined as a separate customs territory a few weeks later.

China's average tariff fell from over 15 per cent to under 10. Foreign companies poured in to build factories along the coast, and exports rose more than fourfold between 2001 and 2008. Economists later described the resulting surge of imports into the United States and Europe as the 'China shock', while hundreds of millions of Chinese moved into industrial and urban jobs.
story.zh:
1986年中国申请恢复关贸总协定缔约国地位（中华民国于1950年退出）。谈判历经天安门事件、1995年世界贸易组织成立，以及与美国、欧盟在农业补贴、银行、电信和汽车关税等问题上的艰苦讨价还价。朱镕基总理顶住国有企业的压力推动达成协议，首席谈判代表龙永图后来自嘲说，谈判谈白了头。

1999年11月中美在北京签署关键的双边协议。2001年11月10日，多哈部长级会议批准中国加入，12月11日正式生效；几周后台湾以"台澎金马单独关税区"名义加入。

中国平均关税从15%以上降到10%以下。外资大量涌入沿海兴建工厂，2001至2008年出口增长逾四倍。经济学家后来把随之而来涌入美欧的进口浪潮称为"中国冲击"，同时数以亿计的中国人进入工业和城市就业。

summary.en: Yang Liwei was launched from the Jiuquan centre in the Gobi on a Long March 2F rocket, orbited the Earth 14 times in about 21 hours and landed in Inner Mongolia. China became the third country, after the Soviet Union and the United States, to put a person in orbit on its own.
summary.zh: 杨利伟乘长征二号F火箭从戈壁中的酒泉卫星发射中心升空，约21小时内绕地球飞行14圈，在内蒙古着陆。中国成为继苏联和美国之后第三个独立将人送入太空的国家。

sources.title: Britannica: Shenzhou
China Manned Space Agency 中国载人航天工程网
中文维基百科：神舟五号

summary.en: A magnitude 7.9 (Chinese scale 8.0) earthquake on the Longmenshan fault struck Wenchuan county at 2:28 pm, killing 69,227 people with 17,923 missing and leaving about five million homeless. The collapse of thousands of schools caused public anger; the relief effort drew huge volunteer support.
summary.zh: 14时28分，四川汶川县龙门山断裂带发生里氏8.0级（矩震级7.9）地震，造成69,227人遇难、17,923人失踪，约五百万人无家可归。大量校舍倒塌引发社会愤慨；抗震救灾吸引了空前规模的志愿者。

sources.title: Britannica: Sichuan earthquake of 2008
USGS: M 7.9 – eastern Sichuan, China, 2008
中文维基百科：汶川地震

story.en:
At 2:28 pm on 12 May 2008 the Longmenshan fault, where the Tibetan Plateau pushes against the Sichuan Basin, ruptured over about 300 kilometres. Towns in the mountain valleys north-west of Chengdu were flattened within two minutes. Beichuan county town was buried by landslides; at Yingxiu near the epicentre most buildings collapsed. Shaking was felt in Beijing and Bangkok.

The quake struck during school hours. Thousands of children died in classroom buildings that collapsed while government offices nearby stood, and parents' protests about poor 'tofu-dreg' construction were censored; the artist Ai Weiwei's attempt to list the children's names led to his harassment. Officials later acknowledged about 5,300 students dead or missing. In one widely reported case, the Sangzao Middle School survived intact because its headmaster had insisted on strengthening its buildings years earlier.

Premier Wen Jiabao flew to the area within hours. Some 130,000 soldiers were deployed, foreign rescue teams were admitted, and tens of thousands of volunteers travelled to Sichuan. Landslide dams created dozens of 'quake lakes', and the Tangjiashan lake above Beichuan had to be drained to avert a flood. The region was rebuilt within three years, partly by pairing each county with a wealthy province.
story.zh:
2008年5月12日14时28分，青藏高原与四川盆地交界处的龙门山断裂带破裂约三百公里。成都西北山谷中的城镇在两分钟内被夷为平地：北川县城被山体滑坡掩埋，震中附近的映秀镇大部分建筑倒塌。北京和曼谷都有震感。

地震发生时正值上课时间。数以千计的孩子死于倒塌的教学楼中，而附近的政府大楼却安然无恙，家长们对"豆腐渣工程"的抗议遭到压制；艺术家艾未未试图统计遇难学生名单，随即受到打压。官方后来承认约五千三百名学生遇难或失踪。另一个广为报道的例子是桑枣中学：因校长多年前坚持加固校舍，全校师生无一伤亡。

温家宝总理在数小时内飞抵灾区。约十三万军人投入救援，国外救援队获准进入，数以万计的志愿者奔赴四川。山体滑坡形成数十个"堰塞湖"，北川上游的唐家山堰塞湖不得不紧急泄洪。灾区在三年内完成重建，采取了"一省帮一县"的对口支援方式。

summary.en: Lee Teng-hui won 54 per cent of the vote in the first direct presidential election in Chinese history, crowning a decade of democratisation that began with the lifting of martial law in 1987. Beijing's missile tests in the Taiwan Strait in the run-up drew two US aircraft carrier groups to the area.
summary.zh: 李登辉在中华民国首次总统直选中获得54%的选票。这是中国历史上第一次由人民直接选举国家元首，标志着自1987年解严以来十年民主化的完成。选前北京在台湾海峡试射导弹，美国派出两个航母战斗群前往附近海域。

sources.title: Britannica: Lee Teng-hui
Shelley Rigger, Politics in Taiwan: Voting for Democracy (1999)
中文维基百科：1996年中华民国总统选举

story.en:
For four decades Taiwan was ruled by the Kuomintang under martial law, with a legislature elected on the mainland in 1947 whose members kept their seats for life. Opposition activists were jailed after the 1979 Kaohsiung Incident, but in 1986 they founded the Democratic Progressive Party in defiance of the ban, and Chiang Ching-kuo let it stand. He lifted martial law in July 1987 and died in January 1988, leaving the presidency to his Taiwan-born vice-president, Lee Teng-hui.

Lee moved carefully. After the Wild Lily student protests of March 1990 he convened a national affairs conference; the 'ten-thousand-year legislators' retired in 1991, and full elections to the legislature followed in 1992. Constitutional amendments in 1994 provided for a directly elected president.

Beijing saw Lee as a covert separatist, especially after his 1995 visit to Cornell University. In July 1995 and again in March 1996, days before the vote, the People's Liberation Army fired missiles into waters near Keelung and Kaohsiung. The United States sent two carrier groups. On 23 March voters gave Lee 54 per cent in a four-way race. In 2000 the DPP's Chen Shui-bian won, the first peaceful transfer of power between parties.
story.zh:
四十年间，国民党在戒严体制下统治台湾，1947年在大陆选出的民意代表终身任职。1979年美丽岛事件后反对派人士被捕入狱，但1986年他们冒禁成立民主进步党，蒋经国未予取缔。1987年7月蒋经国宣布解严，1988年1月去世，由台湾出生的副总统李登辉继任。

李登辉步步为营。1990年3月野百合学运后，他召开国是会议；"万年国代"于1991年全部退职，1992年立法院全面改选。1994年修宪确立总统直选。

北京视李登辉为暗中搞"台独"，1995年他访问母校康奈尔大学后尤甚。1995年7月和1996年3月选举前夕，解放军两度向基隆、高雄附近海域试射导弹，美国派出两个航母战斗群。3月23日，李登辉在四组候选人中以54%的得票率当选。2000年民进党的陈水扁胜选，台湾首次实现政党轮替。
